Ele não cobre (ou cobre com uma questão só): - RAG com Vertex AI Agent Builder, Model Garden, Gemini e fine-tuning de foundation models (1.2, 2.2, 3.2); - avaliação de soluções de IA generativa (2.3); - Colab Enterprise e notebooks no Dataproc (2.2); - endpoints privados, A/B testing e Reduction Server aparecem só uma ou duas vezes. h: Quando praticar: depois de cada curso

x: Nestas o arquivo original marca uma resposta que a revisão considera errada. Vale ler a explicação com atenção, porque são boas pegadinhas. Questão Arquivo Revisado Por quê Q18 (1.3) D C O gabarito D está errado: o AutoML Tables permite indicar uma coluna como Time column, e então faz o split cronológico automaticamente, reservando dados mais recentes para validação e teste. A opção D faz manualmente o que o AutoML já resolve e com intervalos de 30 dias arbitrários; a opção B ignora a ordem temporal e causaria leakage. Q86 (5.3) B D Vertex ML Metadata é o serviço gerenciado para rastrear artefatos, execuções e linhagem, garantindo reprodutibilidade. O gabarito B (Hive Metastore) está errado: ele guarda metadados de tabelas Hive, não metadados de ML; operations suite e BigQuery (A, C) também não são feitos para isso. Q130 (4.2) C B Carregar o modelo diretamente no job Dataflow (por exemplo, via RunInference) elimina a chamada de rede a um serviço externo, o que dá a menor latência possível de serving. O gabarito C (endpoint do Vertex AI) é tentador por ser gerenciado, mas cada predição adiciona um round-trip HTTP; Cloud Run e GKE têm o mesmo problema. Esta é a resposta do conjunto de questões de exemplo do Google. Q167 (1.1) B C O BigQuery ML já faz one-hot encoding automático de colunas STRING no CREATE MODEL, e esse pré-processamento vai junto no modelo exportado, então basta selecionar as features: é o caminho mais rápido. Em B, aplicar ML.ONE HOT ENCODER fora do TRANSFORM

- Leia o enunciado, decida a resposta e só então abra o bloco verde. - Ao errar, anote o conceito do rodapé da resposta: os erros repetidos mostram o que revisar. - Muitas questões usam nomes antigos (AI Platform, Cloud ML Engine). A explicação traz o nome atual; na prova vale o raciocínio, não o nome. - O simulador interativo (https://claude.ai/artifact/3W3WQvvz7danLX4VBWHT1n) sorteia questões por seção ou curso e marca acertos.

- Arquivo de questões enviado por Leonardo em 16/10/2026. - Guia oficial do exame Professional Machine Learning Engineer (versão em vigor desde 01/10/2024). - Revisão e classificação: Claude, 16/10/2026.

You work for a large retailer and have been asked to segment your customers by their purchasing habits. The purchase history of all customers has been uploaded to BigQuery. You suspect that there may be several distinct customer segments, however you are unsure of how many, and you don’t yet understand the commonalities in their behavior. You want to find the most efficient solution. What should you do? Segmentação sem rótulos é clustering; k-means no BigQuery ML roda onde os dados já estão e pode escolher automaticamente o número de clusters. Rotular com Data Labeling Service e treinar AutoML (C, D) transforma um problema não supervisionado em supervisionado sem rótulos válidos. BigQuery ML, k-means, clustering

You need to train a regression model based on a dataset containing 50,000 records that is stored in BigQuery. The data includes a total of 20 categorical and numerical features with a target variable that can include negative values. You need to minimize effort and training time while maximizing model performance. What approach should you take to train this regression model? Com 50 mil registros já no BigQuery, XGBoost (boosted tree regressor) no BigQuery ML treina rápido, com pouco esforço e boa performance em dados tabulares. AutoML (C, D) leva no mínimo cerca de uma hora, e RMSLE não serve para target com valores negativos. BigQuery ML, XGBoost, regressão

You have been given a dataset with sales predictions based on your company’s marketing activities. The data is structured and stored in BigQuery, and has been carefully managed by a team of data analysts. You need to prepare a report providing insights into the predictive capabilities of the data. You were asked to run several ML models with different levels of sophistication, including simple models and multilayered neural networks. You only have a few hours to gather the results of your experiments. Which Google Cloud tools should you use to complete this task in the most efficient and self-serviced way? Os dados estruturados já estão no BigQuery, e o BigQuery ML permite treinar em poucas horas, via SQL, de modelos lineares a DNN, com avaliação integrada e de forma self-service. Notebooks com scikit-learn (C) são tentadores, mas exigem mover dados e escrever mais código. BigQuery ML, self-service, prototipagem rápida

You are a data scientist at an industrial equipment manufacturing company. You are developing a regression model to estimate the power consumption in the company’s manufacturing plants based on sensor data collected from all of the plants. The sensors collect tens of millions of records every day. You need to schedule daily training runs for your model that use all the data collected up to the current date. You want your model to scale smoothly and require minimal development work. What should you do? Dezenas de milhões de registros por dia com retreino diário agendado sobre todo o histórico: o BigQuery ML escala nativamente, tem scheduled queries e exige o mínimo de desenvolvimento. Modelos custom em Vertex AI Training (B, C) exigem mais código, e AutoML (A) é mais caro e lento para retreino diário. BigQuery ML, retreino agendado, escalabilidade

You are a data scientist at an industrial equipment manufacturing company. You are developing a regression model to estimate the power consumption in the company’s manufacturing plants based on sensor data collected from all of the plants. The sensors collect tens of millions of records every day. You need to schedule daily training runs for your model that use all the data collected up to the current date. You want your model to scale smoothly and require minimal development work. What should you do? BigQuery ML treina direto onde os dados estão, escala com grandes volumes e pode ser agendado com scheduled queries com mínimo desenvolvimento. Modelos custom em TF, PyTorch ou scikit-learn no Vertex AI Training (A, C, D) exigem mais código e pipeline de dados. BigQuery ML, regression, scheduled queries

You are working with a dataset that contains customer transactions. You need to build an ML model to predict customer purchase behavior. You plan to develop the model in BigQuery ML, and export it to Cloud Storage for online prediction. You notice that the input data contains a few categorical features, including product category and payment method. You want to deploy the model as quickly as possible. What should you do? O BigQuery ML já faz one-hot encoding automático de colunas STRING no CREATE MODEL, e esse pré-processamento vai junto no modelo exportado, então basta selecionar as features: é o caminho mais rápido. Em B, aplicar ML.ONE HOT ENCODER fora do TRANSFORM obriga a replicar o encoding no serving, o que gera risco de skew e mais trabalho; por isso discordo do gabarito. A funciona, mas é passo desnecessário. BigQuery ML, one-hot encoding, TRANSFORM, model export

You work for an online retailer. Your company has a few thousand short lifecycle products. Your company has five years of sales data stored in BigQuery. You have been asked to build a model that will make monthly sales predictions for each product. You want to use a solution that can be implemented quickly with minimal effort. What should you do? O ARIMA PLUS do BigQuery ML treina, com uma única instrução SQL, milhares de séries temporais (uma por produto) diretamente onde os dados estão, sendo a solução mais rápida e com menor esforço. Vertex AI Forecast (B) também é gerenciado, mas exige exportar/configurar o dataset e tem treino mais demorado e caro; Prophet ou TensorFlow customizados (A, D) exigem código. BigQuery ML, ARIMA PLUS, forecasting, séries temporais

You work for a large retailer, and you need to build a model to predict customer chum. The company has a dataset of historical customer data, including customer demographics purchase history, and website activity. You need to create the model in BigQuery ML and thoroughly evaluate its performance. What should you do? Churn é classificação binária, então se usa logistic regression; registrar o modelo do BigQuery ML no Vertex AI Model Registry dá acesso à avaliação completa no Vertex AI (curvas, matriz de confusão, métricas por threshold). Linear regression (A, C) é para valores contínuos, e ML.CONFUSION MATRIX (D) sozinho não é uma avaliação completa. BigQuery ML, logistic regression, Model Registry, avaliação

You work for a company that sells corporate electronic products to thousands of businesses worldwide. Your company stores historical customer data in BigQuery. You need to build a model that predicts customer lifetime value over the next three years. You want to use the simplest approach to build the model and you want to have access to visualization tools. What should you do? Rodar CREATE MODEL com AutoML direto no console do BigQuery e validar com ML.EVALUATE/ML.PREDICT é o caminho mais simples, sem mover dados nem criar notebooks; o console mostra gráficos de avaliação do modelo. As alternativas com Workbench adicionam etapas (EDA, tabelas intermediárias, CSV) que contrariam o requisito de simplicidade. BigQuery ML, AutoML, ML.EVALUATE, CLV

You work at a gaming startup that has several terabytes of structured data in Cloud Storage. This data includes gameplay time data, user metadata, and game metadata. You want to build a model that recommends new games to users that requires the least amount of coding. What should you do? Matrix factorization do BigQuery ML é o modelo de recomendação nativo, treinado com SQL, exigindo o mínimo de código. Two-tower ou matrix factorization em TensorFlow (C/D) exigem muito mais código, e autoencoder (A) não é o modelo padrão de recomendação. BigQuery ML, matrix factorization, recommendation

You are designing an ML recommendation model for shoppers on your company's ecommerce website. You will use Recommendations AI to build, test, and deploy your system. How should you develop recommendations that increase revenue while following best practices? O tipo "Frequently Bought Together" é recomendado para aumentar o tamanho do carrinho e, portanto, a receita. "Others You May Like" (A) otimiza engajamento/CTR, não receita por pedido; importar eventos antes do catálogo (C) ou usar catálogo falso (D) contraria as boas práticas. Recommendations AI, recommendation types, retail

You are designing an architecture with a serverless ML system to enrich customer support tickets with informative metadata before they are routed to a support agent. You need a set of models to predict ticket priority, predict ticket resolution time, and perform sentiment analysis to help agents make strategic decisions when they process support requests. Tickets are not expected to have any domain-specific terms or jargon. The proposed architecture has the following flow: Which endpoints should the Enrichment Cloud Functions call? Prioridade e tempo de resolução são previsões específicas do negócio e exigem modelos customizados, enquanto sentimento sem jargão de domínio é atendido pela Cloud Natural Language API pré-treinada. AutoML Natural Language (B) seria esforço desnecessário, e as opções com Vision não fazem sentido para texto. Natural Language API, sentiment analysis, custom models

You work for a company that is developing a new video streaming platform. You have been asked to create a recommendation system that will suggest the next video for a user to watch. After a review by an AI Ethics team, you are approved to start development. Each video asset in your company’s catalog has useful metadata (e.g., content type, release date, country), but you do not have any historical user event data. How should you build the recommendation system for the first version of the product? Sem dados de eventos de usuário, a abordagem recomendada (Rules of ML) é lançar com heurísticas baseadas em metadata e coletar dados para um modelo futuro. Treinar com MovieLens (C) não transfere para outro catálogo, e embeddings via autoencoder (D) são complexidade sem dado que valide o resultado. cold start, recommendation, heuristics

Your company stores a large number of audio files of phone calls made to your customer call center in an on-premises database. Each audio file is in wav format and is approximately 5 minutes long. You need to analyze these audio files for customer sentiment. You plan to use the Speech-to-Text API You want to use the most efficient approach. What should you do? Áudios de 5 minutos passam do limite de cerca de 1 minuto do recognize síncrono, então o caminho é subir para o Cloud Storage e usar longrunningrecognize; a Natural Language API analyzeSentiment é pré-treinada e não exige treinar modelo. AutoML (A, C) é desnecessário, e enviar o conteúdo local inline (D) é menos eficiente e tem limite de tamanho. Speech-to-Text, Natural Language API, sentiment analysis

You work for a company that captures live video footage of checkout areas in their retail stores. You need to use the live video footage to build a model to detect the number of customers waiting for service in near real time. You want to implement a solution quickly and with minimal effort. How should you build the model? O modelo Occupancy Analytics do Vertex AI Vision é pré-treinado para contar pessoas/veículos em zonas e filas de vídeo ao vivo, entregando a contagem quase em tempo real sem treino. O Person/vehicle detector (B) apenas detecta objetos e exigiria lógica extra de contagem por zona; treinar AutoML (C, D) é mais lento e trabalhoso. Vertex AI Vision, Occupancy Analytics, vídeo em streaming

You work for a hotel and have a dataset that contains customers’ written comments scanned from paper-based customer feedback forms, which are stored as PDF files. Every form has the same layout. You need to quickly predict an overall satisfaction score from the customer comments on each form. How should you accomplish this task? Como todos os formulários têm o mesmo layout, um Document AI custom extractor isola o texto da seção de comentários com precisão, e analyzeSentiment da Natural Language API devolve o sentimento geral do documento, que mapeia para a satisfação geral. Vision API OCR (A) extrai o texto da página inteira, misturando campos irrelevantes; analyzeEntitySentiment (B, D) dá sentimento por entidade, não um score global. Document AI, custom extractor, Natural Language API, analyzeSentiment

You work for a pet food company that manages an online forum. Customers upload photos of their pets on the forum to share with others. About 20 photos are uploaded daily. You want to automatically and in near real time detect whether each uploaded photo has an animal. You want to prioritize time and minimize cost of your application development and deployment. What should you do? Com apenas cerca de 20 fotos por dia, a Cloud Vision API (object localization ou labels) detecta animais sem treino, sem infraestrutura e com custo por uso mínimo. Deployar um modelo do TensorFlow Hub (B) gera custo fixo de endpoint, e treinar AutoML com rotulagem manual (C, D) consome muito tempo. Cloud Vision API, object localization, APIs pré-treinadas

You work for an international manufacturing organization that ships scientific products all over the world. Instruction manuals for these products need to be translated to 15 different languages. Your organization’s leadership team wants to start using machine learning to reduce the cost of manual human translations and increase translation speed. You need to implement a scalable solution that maximizes accuracy and minimizes operational overhead. You also want to include a process to evaluate and fix incorrect translations. What should you do? AutoML Translation treinado com dados do domínio maximiza a qualidade, e o Translation Hub gerencia a tradução de documentos em vários idiomas com fluxo de pós-edição por revisores humanos, minimizando overhead. Cloud Functions com a Translation API genérica (A) é menos precisa e exige montar o fluxo; B e D são complexos demais. AutoML Translation, Translation Hub, human-in-the-loop

ou work at an organization that maintains a cloud-based communication platform that integrates conventional chat, voice, and video conferencing into one platform. The audio recordings are stored in Cloud Storage. All recordings have an 8 kHz sample rate and are more than one minute long. You need to implement a new feature in the platform that will automatically transcribe voice call recordings into a text for future applications, such as call summarization and sentiment analysis. How should you implement the voice call transcription feature following Google-recommended best practices? A boa prática do Speech-to-Text é usar a taxa de amostragem nativa (sem resampling, que não melhora a qualidade e pode piorar) e, para áudios com mais de um minuto, usar reconhecimento assíncrono (LongRunningRecognize). Upsample para 16 kHz (D) é tentador porque 16 kHz é o recomendado na captura, mas reamostrar áudio já gravado em 8 kHz não acrescenta informação. Speech-to-Text, asynchronous recognition, sample rate

You work for a multinational organization that has recently begun operations in Spain. Teams within your organization will need to work with various Spanish documents, such as business, legal, and financial documents. You want to use machine learning to help your organization get accurate translations quickly and with the least effort. Your organization does not require domain-specific terms or jargon. What should you do? A Document Translation da Cloud Translation API traduz documentos inteiros mantendo formatação, sem treino, com o mínimo de esforço, o que basta já que não há jargão de domínio. AutoML Translation (B) só se justifica com terminologia específica, e modelos próprios (A/D) são esforço excessivo. Cloud Translation API, Document Translation, pre-trained API

You need to build classification workflows over several structured datasets currently stored in BigQuery. Because you will be performing the classification several times, you want to complete the following steps without writing code: exploratory data analysis, feature selection, model building, training, and hyperparameter tuning and serving. What should you do? AutoML Tables cobre EDA, seleção de features, treino, tuning e serving sem escrever código. BigQuery ML (B) exige escrever SQL e não faz feature selection e tuning de forma totalmente automática; notebooks e AI Platform exigem código. AutoML, tabular, no-code

You work for a large hotel chain and have been asked to assist the marketing team in gathering predictions for a targeted marketing strategy. You need to make predictions about user lifetime value (LTV) over the next 20 days so that marketing can be adjusted accordingly. The customer dataset is in BigQuery, and you are preparing the tabular data for training with AutoML Tables. This data has a time signal that is spread across multiple columns. How should you ensure that AutoML fits the best model to your data? O gabarito D está errado: o AutoML Tables permite indicar uma coluna como Time column, e então faz o split cronológico automaticamente, reservando dados mais recentes para validação e teste. A opção D faz manualmente o que o AutoML já resolve e com intervalos de 30 dias arbitrários; a opção B ignora a ordem temporal e causaria leakage. AutoML, time column, data split, leakage

You work for a large technology company that wants to modernize their contact center. You have been asked to develop a solution to classify incoming calls by product so that requests can be more quickly routed to the correct support team. You have already transcribed the calls using the Speech-to-Text API. You want to minimize data preprocessing and development time. How should you build the model? AutoML Natural Language treina um extrator de entidades customizadas (produtos) com pouco preparo de dados e desenvolvimento. A Cloud Natural Language API (C) é tentadora, mas não extrai entidades customizadas do domínio da empresa. AutoML, entity extraction, Natural Language

You work for a credit card company and have been asked to create a custom fraud detection model based on historical data using AutoML Tables. You need to prioritize detection of fraudulent transactions while minimizing false positives. Which optimization objective should you use when training the model? Em fraude o dataset é muito desbalanceado e o foco é a classe positiva rara; AUC PR otimiza o trade-off entre precision e recall nessa classe. AUC ROC (D) é tentadora, mas fica otimista em dados desbalanceados por causa dos muitos verdadeiros negativos. AutoML Tables, AUC PR, desbalanceamento

You have a large corpus of written support cases that can be classified into 3 separate categories: Technical Support, Billing Support, or Other Issues. You need to quickly build, test, and deploy a service that will automatically classify future written requests into one of the categories. How should you configure the pipeline? Categorias customizadas e necessidade de rapidez apontam para AutoML de texto, que treina, avalia e implanta como endpoint REST sem código de modelagem. A Natural Language API (A) só tem categorias predefinidas; BERT custom (D) é mais trabalhoso. AutoML, classificação de texto, low-code

You need to quickly build and train a model to predict the sentiment of customer reviews with custom categories without writing code. You do not have enough data to train a model from scratch. The resulting model should have high predictive performance. Which service should you use? AutoML Natural Language treina sentimento com categorias customizadas sem código e usa transfer learning, funcionando com poucos dados. A Natural Language API (B) não aceita categorias customizadas de sentimento. AutoML, sentiment analysis, no-code

You need to build classification workflows over several structured datasets currently stored in BigQuery. Because you will be performing the classification several times, you want to complete the following steps without writing code: exploratory data analysis, feature selection, model building, training, and hyperparameter tuning and serving. What should you do? Vertex AutoML tabular cobre EDA, seleção de features, treino, hyperparameter tuning e serving sem escrever código, lendo direto do BigQuery. BigQuery ML (C) é tentador, mas exige escrever SQL e não automatiza todo o fluxo; as opções com TensorFlow e scikit-learn exigem código. AutoML, tabular, no-code

You need to build classification workflows over several structured datasets currently stored in BigQuery. Because you will be performing the classification several times, you want to complete the following steps without writing code: exploratory data analysis, feature selection, model building, training, and hyperparameter tuning and serving. What should you do? AutoML tabular faz EDA, feature selection, treino, tuning e serving sem código, direto a partir do BigQuery. BigQuery ML (C) exige SQL e escolhas manuais, e TensorFlow ou scikit-learn (A, D) exigem código. AutoML, tabular classification, no-code

You want to train an AutoML model to predict house prices by using a small public dataset stored in BigQuery. You need to prepare the data and want to use the simplest, most efficient approach. What should you do? Pré-processar com SQL no BigQuery e criar o Vertex AI managed dataset direto da tabela é o caminho mais simples, sem exportar arquivos. Exportar CSV (C, D) ou usar Dataflow com TFRecord (B) adiciona passos desnecessários, e AutoML tabular nem consome TFRecord. AutoML, BigQuery, managed dataset

You need to develop an image classification model by using a large dataset that contains labeled images in a Cloud Storage bucket. What should you do? Para classificação de imagens com dataset rotulado no Cloud Storage, importar como managed dataset e usar AutoML é a solução gerenciada e de menor esforço. Pipelines com KFP ou TFX (A, B) exigem código custom, e converter imagens em tabela para o BigQuery ML (D) não faz sentido. AutoML Image, managed dataset, Cloud Storage

You work for a retail company. You have a managed tabular dataset in Vertex AI that contains sales data from three different stores. The dataset includes several features, such as store name and sale timestamp. You want to use the data to train a model that makes sales predictions for a new store that will open soon. You need to split the data between the training, validation, and test sets. What approach should you use to split the data? Para previsão de vendas, o split cronológico pelo timestamp evita leakage temporal e reflete o uso real do modelo. O split manual por loja (A) é tentador por simular uma loja nova, mas com só três lojas deixaria uma única loja para treino, com dados insuficientes. Splits aleatórios (B, D) vazam informação do futuro. data split, chronological split, Vertex AI datasets

You work for an auto insurance company. You are preparing a proof-of-concept ML application that uses images of damaged vehicles to infer damaged parts. Your team has assembled a set of annotated images from damage claim documents in the company’s database. The annotations associated with each image consist of a bounding box for each identified damaged part and the part name. You have been given a sufficient budget to train models on Google Cloud. You need to quickly create an initial model. What should you do? AutoML Object Detection no Vertex AI treina um modelo inicial a partir das imagens anotadas com bounding boxes sem escrever código, o caminho mais rápido para uma PoC. Fine-tuning de modelo do TensorFlow Hub (A) ou custom training (D) exigem código, e montar um pipeline com AutoMLTrainingJobRunOp (C) adiciona complexidade desnecessária para um primeiro modelo. AutoML, object detection, Vertex AI, PoC

You work for a hospital that wants to optimize how it schedules operations. You need to create a model that uses the relationship between the number of surgeries scheduled and beds used. You want to predict how many beds will be needed for patients each day in advance based on the scheduled surgeries. You have one year of data for the hospital organized in 365 rows. The data includes the following variables for each day: • Number of scheduled surgeries • Number of beds occupied • Date You want to maximize the speed of model development and testing. What should you do? O problema é de série temporal em que o número de cirurgias agendadas é conhecido antecipadamente, então o AutoML Forecasting com esse valor como covariate conhecida no futuro e a data como time column modela diretamente a demanda diária de leitos com pouco esforço. A regressão em BigQuery ML (A) é uma alternativa forte e mais rápida de treinar, por isso parte da comunidade a escolhe; ARIMA (B) ignora a variável de cirurgias e C usa apenas cirurgias 'menores', descartando informação. AutoML Forecasting, covariates, séries temporais, BigQuery ML

You work at a leading healthcare firm developing state-of-the-art algorithms for various use cases. You have unstructured textual data with custom labels. You need to extract and classify various medical phrases with these labels. What should you do? Como os rótulos são customizados, AutoML Entity Extraction treina um extrator com as labels próprias sem precisar de código. A Healthcare Natural Language API (A) é tentadora, mas só extrai entidades médicas com sua taxonomia fixa, sem suportar labels customizadas; BERT ou TensorFlow customizados (B, D) exigem muito mais esforço. AutoML, entity extraction, labels customizadas, Healthcare Natural Language API

You work for a company that is developing an application to help users with meal planning. You want to use machine learning to scan a corpus of recipes and extract each ingredient (e.g., carrot, rice, pasta) and each kitchen cookware (e.g., bowl, pot, spoon) mentioned. Each recipe is saved in an unstructured text file. What should you do? Entity extraction com AutoML e duas entidades ('ingredient' e 'cookware') com exemplos rotulados é o que o problema pede: extrair menções em texto não estruturado. A Entity Analysis da Natural Language API (C) não reconhece essas categorias customizadas; criar uma entidade por ingrediente (D) é inviável. AutoML, entity extraction, NLP

You work for a semiconductor manufacturing company. You need to create a real-time application that automates the quality control process. High-definition images of each semiconductor are taken at the end of the assembly line in real time. The photos are uploaded to a Cloud Storage bucket along with tabular data that includes each semiconductor’s batch number, serial number, dimensions, and weight. You need to configure model training and serving while maximizing model accuracy. What should you do? Rotular as imagens e treinar um modelo AutoML de classificação de imagens maximiza a acurácia para inspeção visual, e o deploy online com Pub/Sub atende o requisito de tempo real. Batch diário (B) não é real-time, K-means não supervisionado (C) perde acurácia, e os dados tabulares (D) não capturam defeitos visuais. AutoML, image classification, Pub/Sub, data labeling

You want to rebuild your ML pipeline for structured data on Google Cloud. You are using PySpark to conduct data transformations at scale, but your pipelines are taking over 12 hours to run. To speed up development and pipeline run time, you want to use a serverless tool and SQL syntax. You have already moved your raw data into Cloud Storage. How should you build the pipeline on Google Cloud while meeting the speed and processing requirements? Carregar os dados no BigQuery e reescrever as transformações em SQL atende aos requisitos de serverless, SQL e velocidade. Dataproc com SparkSQL (B) usa SQL mas não é serverless no sentido pedido, e Cloud SQL (C) não escala para esse volume analítico. BigQuery, SQL, serverless, ETL

You are building a real-time prediction engine that streams files which may contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII) to Google Cloud. You want to use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP) API to scan the files. How should you ensure that the PII is not accessible by unauthorized individuals? O padrão de quarentena mantém os dados num bucket isolado até o DLP classificá-los, e só então move para buckets sensível ou não sensível, evitando exposição. Escrever direto no bucket não sensível (C) ou no BigQuery (A, B) deixa o PII acessível antes da varredura. Cloud DLP, PII, quarantine bucket

Your organization's call center has asked you to develop a model that analyzes customer sentiments in each call. The call center receives over one million calls daily, and data is stored in Cloud Storage. The data collected must not leave the region in which the call originated, and no Personally Identifiable Information (PII) can be stored or analyzed. The data science team has a third-party tool for visualization and access which requires a SQL ANSI-2011 compliant interface. You need to select components for data processing and for analytics. How should the data pipeline be designed? Dataflow processa o volume de chamadas na região de origem e pode remover PII (com DLP), e o BigQuery oferece interface SQL ANSI 2011 escalável para a ferramenta de visualização. Cloud SQL (C) é tentador pelo SQL, mas não escala bem para analytics desse volume. Dataflow, BigQuery, data residency, PII

You are responsible for building a unified analytics environment across a variety of on-premises data marts. Your company is experiencing data quality and security challenges when integrating data across the servers, caused by the use of a wide range of disconnected tools and temporary solutions. You need a fully managed, cloud-native data integration service that will lower the total cost of work and reduce repetitive work. Some members on your team prefer a codeless interface for building Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) process. Which service should you use? Cloud Data Fusion é o serviço gerenciado de integração de dados com interface visual sem código para ETL e muitos conectores para fontes on-premises. Dataprep (B) é tentador pela interface visual, mas foca em preparo e limpeza de dados, não em integração de várias fontes. Cloud Data Fusion, ETL, no-code

You have a demand forecasting pipeline in production that uses Dataflow to preprocess raw data prior to model training and prediction. During preprocessing, you employ Z-score normalization on data stored in BigQuery and write it back to BigQuery. New training data is added every week. You want to make the process more efficient by minimizing computation time and manual intervention. What should you do? Fazer a normalização Z-score diretamente em SQL no BigQuery elimina o round trip via Dataflow, reduzindo tempo de computação e manutenção. O normalizer fn (C) é tentador, mas move a lógica para o modelo e não reduz o pipeline de pré-processamento existente. BigQuery, SQL, normalization

You recently joined an enterprise-scale company that has thousands of datasets. You know that there are accurate descriptions for each table in BigQuery, and you are searching for the proper BigQuery table to use for a model you are building on AI Platform. How should you find the data that you need? Data Catalog permite buscar ativos do BigQuery por palavras-chave nas descrições, ideal para milhares de datasets. INFORMATION SCHEMA (D) é tentador, mas é limitado ao escopo consultado e não é uma ferramenta de descoberta. Data Catalog, data discovery, metadata

You are working on a Neural Network-based project. The dataset provided to you has columns with different ranges. While preparing the data for model training, you discover that gradient optimization is having difficulty moving weights to a good solution. What should you do? Features em escalas muito diferentes deixam a superfície de perda mal condicionada e atrapalham o gradient descent; normalizar resolve. Feature construction (A) ou remover features (C) não atacam a diferença de escala. normalização, gradient descent, feature scaling

While conducting an exploratory analysis of a dataset, you discover that categorical feature A has substantial predictive power, but it is sometimes missing. What should you do? Criar uma categoria 'missing' e uma flag binária preserva a informação de ausência, que pode ser preditiva, sem descartar a feature forte. Imputar pela moda (B) é tentador, mas mascara o padrão de ausência e introduz viés. missing values, feature engineering, categóricas

Your company manages an application that aggregates news articles from many different online sources and sends them to users. You need to build a recommendation model that will suggest articles to readers that are similar to the articles they are currently reading. Which approach should you use? Recomendar artigos parecidos com o que se está lendo é content-based: embeddings (word2vec) mais similaridade vetorial. Collaborative filtering (A) é tentador, mas recomenda pelo comportamento do usuário, não pela similaridade de conteúdo. embeddings, similaridade vetorial, recomendação content-based

You are building a linear regression model on BigQuery ML to predict a customer’s likelihood of purchasing your company’s products. Your model uses a city name variable as a key predictive component. In order to train and serve the model, your data must be organized in columns. You want to prepare your data using the least amount of coding while maintaining the predictable variables. What should you do? One-hot encoding transforma a variável categórica cidade em colunas binárias sem perder poder preditivo, e o Dataprep faz isso visualmente com pouco código. Agrupar cidades em regiões numeradas (C) cria uma ordinalidade falsa e perde informação; remover a coluna (B) descarta o preditor. Dataprep, one-hot encoding, feature engineering

You need to analyze user activity data from your company’s mobile applications. Your team will use BigQuery for data analysis, transformation, and experimentation with ML algorithms. You need to ensure real-time ingestion of the user activity data into BigQuery. What should you do? Pub/Sub tem BigQuery subscriptions que gravam mensagens direto no BigQuery em tempo real, sem pipeline extra, o que é a solução de menor esforço quando não há transformação. Pub/Sub + Dataflow (D) é tentador por ser o padrão clássico, mas adiciona componentes desnecessários já que as transformações serão feitas no BigQuery. Pub/Sub, BigQuery subscription, streaming ingestion

You are building an ML model to predict trends in the stock market based on a wide range of factors. While exploring the data, you notice that some features have a large range. You want to ensure that the features with the largest magnitude don’t overfit the model. What should you do? Normalizar as features para [0,1] coloca todas na mesma escala, evitando que features de grande magnitude dominem o treino. A transformação logarítmica (A) é tentadora para distribuições assimétricas, mas não garante escala comum; PCA (B) e binning (C) mudam a representação e podem perder informação. normalização, feature scaling, pré-processamento

You are developing an ML model to predict house prices. While preparing the data, you discover that an important predictor variable, distance from the closest school, is often missing and does not have high variance. Every instance (row) in your data is important. How should you handle the missing data? Como todas as linhas são importantes, não se pode removê-las; imputar os valores com um modelo de regressão linear a partir das outras features preserva os dados com estimativas razoáveis. Substituir por zero (D) é tentador por ser simples, mas zero é uma distância irreal e distorce a feature; feature cross (B) não resolve ausência. missing values, imputação, regressão linear

While performing exploratory data analysis on a dataset, you find that an important categorical feature has 5% null values. You want to minimize the bias that could result from the missing values. How should you handle the missing values? Para uma feature categórica, criar a categoria 'missing' preserva as linhas e permite ao modelo aprender se a ausência é informativa, minimizando viés. Substituir pela média (B) é tentador, mas não faz sentido para variáveis categóricas; remover linhas (A) pode introduzir viés se os dados não faltam ao acaso. missing values, feature categórica, viés

You work on a data science team at a bank and are creating an ML model to predict loan default risk. You have collected and cleaned hundreds of millions of records worth of training data in a BigQuery table, and you now want to develop and compare multiple models on this data using TensorFlow and Vertex AI. You want to minimize any bottlenecks during the data ingestion state while considering scalability. What should you do? O TensorFlow I/O BigQuery Reader lê os dados diretamente do BigQuery em paralelo via Storage Read API, sem etapa de exportação, escalando para centenas de milhões de registros. Converter em TFRecords (C) é tentador por ser o formato ideal do TensorFlow, mas exige um passo extra de exportação/conversão e duplica dados; carregar em dataframe (A) não cabe em memória. TensorFlow I/O, BigQuery Storage API, tf.data

You work on a data science team at a bank and are creating an ML model to predict loan default risk. You have collected and cleaned hundreds of millions of records worth of training data in a BigQuery table, and you now want to develop and compare multiple models on this data using TensorFlow and Vertex AI. You want to minimize any bottlenecks during the data ingestion state while considering scalability. What should you do? Questão duplicada da anterior: o TensorFlow I/O BigQuery Reader lê do BigQuery diretamente e em paralelo, minimizando gargalos de ingestão com boa escalabilidade. TFRecords (C) é tentador, mas exige exportação e conversão adicionais; CSV com TextLineDataset (B) é lento para parsear. TensorFlow I/O, BigQuery, ingestão de dados

You work for the AI team of an automobile company, and you are developing a visual defect detection model using TensorFlow and Keras. To improve your model performance, you want to incorporate some image augmentation functions such as translation, cropping, and contrast tweaking. You randomly apply these functions to each training batch. You want to optimize your data processing pipeline for run time and compute resources utilization. What should you do? Aplicar as augmentations dentro do pipeline tf.data roda em paralelo com o treino (com map paralelo e prefetch), aproveitando melhor CPU e acelerador sem armazenar dados extras. Keras generators (B) são tentadores, mas rodam em Python single-threaded e são mais lentos; pré-gerar com Dataflow (C, D) consome armazenamento e perde a aleatoriedade por época. tf.data, data augmentation, input pipeline

You work on the data science team at a manufacturing company. You are reviewing the company’s historical sales data, which has hundreds of millions of records. For your exploratory data analysis, you need to calculate descriptive statistics such as mean, median, and mode; conduct complex statistical tests for hypothesis testing; and plot variations of the features over time. You want to use as much of the sales data as possible in your analyses while minimizing computational resources. What should you do? Calcular estatísticas descritivas direto no BigQuery evita mover centenas de milhões de linhas e usa o motor serverless, e o notebook fica só com os testes estatísticos e plots sobre resultados agregados. Importar todo o dataset para o notebook (A, B) desperdiça memória e compute. D é tentadora, mas espalhar a análise por três ferramentas não reduz recursos de forma relevante em relação a C. BigQuery, EDA, Vertex AI Workbench

You are training an ML model using data stored in BigQuery that contains several values that are considered Personally Identifiable Information (PII). You need to reduce the sensitivity of the dataset before training your model. Every column is critical to your model. How should you proceed? Cloud DLP identifica os dados sensíveis e a Format Preserving Encryption pseudonimiza preservando formato e consistência, então as colunas continuam úteis ao modelo. Randomizar (A) destrói o sinal, e remover colunas (D) contraria o requisito de que todas são críticas. AES-256 com salt (C) gera valores sem formato e não consistentes para o treino. Cloud DLP, Format Preserving Encryption, PII, Dataflow

You are developing an ML model using a dataset with categorical input variables. You have randomly split half of the data into training and test sets. After applying one-hot encoding on the categorical variables in the training set, you discover that one categorical variable is missing from the test set. What should you do? O mesmo one-hot encoding (com o vocabulário aprendido no treino) precisa ser aplicado ao test set para que as features tenham o mesmo formato. Re-split (B) ou coletar mais dados (D) não resolvem o problema real, que é a transformação inconsistente entre treino e teste. one-hot encoding, train/test consistency, preprocessing

You are analyzing customer data for a healthcare organization that is stored in Cloud Storage. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). You need to perform data exploration and preprocessing while ensuring the security and privacy of sensitive fields. What should you do? A Cloud DLP API (Sensitive Data Protection) de-identifica a PII (mascaramento, tokenização) antes da exploração, de modo que os analistas nunca veem os dados sensíveis. CMEK ou chaves gerenciadas pelo Google (B, D) protegem os dados em repouso, mas os dados ficam expostos depois de descriptografados; VPC Service Controls (C) evita exfiltração mas não protege os campos sensíveis. Cloud DLP, de-identificação, PII, Sensitive Data Protection

You are using Keras and TensorFlow to develop a fraud detection model. Records of customer transactions are stored in a large table in BigQuery. You need to preprocess these records in a cost-effective and efficient way before you use them to train the model. The trained model will be used to perform batch inference in BigQuery. How should you implement the preprocessing workflow? Pré-processar com SQL no próprio BigQuery é eficiente e barato, e ler diretamente com o BigQuery reader do TensorFlow evita exportar arquivos; como a inferência em lote também será no BigQuery, a lógica fica consistente. Dataflow ou Dataproc gerando CSVs (A, D) adicionam custo e etapas, e pandas (B) não escala para uma tabela grande. BigQuery, pré-processamento SQL, TensorFlow I/O, custo

You need to use TensorFlow to train an image classification model. Your dataset is located in a Cloud Storage directory and contains millions of labeled images. Before training the model, you need to prepare the data. You want the data preprocessing and model training workflow to be as efficient, scalable, and low maintenance as possible. What should you do? Um job de Dataflow que gera TFRecords fragmentados no Cloud Storage escala para milhões de imagens, e o tf.data.TFRecordDataset lê esses shards com alto throughput no Vertex AI Training gerenciado. Organizar pastas por label e usar ImageFolder (B) lê milhões de arquivos pequenos, com baixa eficiência de I/O; fazer tudo em uma instância do Workbench (C, D) não escala e exige mais manutenção. TFRecord, Dataflow, tf.data, Vertex AI Training

You work for a delivery company. You need to design a system that stores and manages features such as parcels delivered and truck locations over time. The system must retrieve the features with low latency and feed those features into a model for online prediction. The data science team will retrieve historical data at a specific point in time for model training. You want to store the features with minimal effort. What should you do? Vertex AI Feature Store oferece serving online de baixa latência e recuperação point-in-time de dados históricos para treino, com mínimo esforço. Bigtable ou BigQuery exigiriam implementar manualmente a lógica de point-in-time e de serving. Vertex AI Feature Store, point-in-time, online serving

You are developing a custom TensorFlow classification model based on tabular data. Your raw data is stored in BigQuery. contains hundreds of millions of rows, and includes both categorical and numerical features. You need to use a MaxMin scaler on some numerical features, and apply a one-hot encoding to some categorical features such as SKU names. Your model will be trained over multiple epochs. You want to minimize the effort and cost of your solution. What should you do? Com centenas de milhões de linhas e treino em várias épocas, aplicar MinMax e one-hot uma única vez com TFX (TensorFlow Transform) no Dataflow e gravar TFRecords evita recomputar as transformações a cada época e garante consistência treino/serving. A opção B é tentadora pela simplicidade, mas deixa o one-hot de um vocabulário grande (SKUs) para o TensorFlow a cada época, aumentando custo e tempo. TensorFlow Transform, Dataflow, TFRecord, feature engineering

You have been asked to build a model using a dataset that is stored in a medium-sized (~10 GB) BigQuery table. You need to quickly determine whether this data is suitable for model development. You want to create a one-time report that includes both informative visualizations of data distributions and more sophisticated statistical analyses to share with other ML engineers on your team. You require maximum flexibility to create your report. What should you do? Maximum flexibility para combinar visualizações e análises estatísticas sofisticadas aponta para notebooks no Vertex AI Workbench, conectados ao BigQuery. Data Studio (B) é tentador para relatórios compartilháveis, mas é limitado para análises estatísticas avançadas; TFDV e Dataprep (C, D) têm escopo fixo. Vertex AI Workbench, EDA, notebooks

You work for a bank with strict data governance requirements. You recently implemented a custom model to detect fraudulent transactions. You want your training code to download internal data by using an API endpoint hosted in your project’s network. You need the data to be accessed in the most secure way, while mitigating the risk of data exfiltration. What should you do? VPC Service Controls cria um perímetro que impede a exfiltração de dados, e com peering o job do Vertex AI acessa o endpoint interno da rede do projeto. É o mecanismo recomendado pelo Google para esse risco. O proxy Cloud Run com IAM (B) controla quem acessa, mas não impede que os dados saiam do perímetro, por isso a escolha é A. VPC Service Controls, data exfiltration, VPC peering

You work for a startup that has multiple data science workloads. Your compute infrastructure is currently on-premises, and the data science workloads are native to PySpark. Your team plans to migrate their data science workloads to Google Cloud. You need to build a proof of concept to migrate one data science job to Google Cloud. You want to propose a migration process that requires minimal cost and effort. What should you do first? Para um job nativo em PySpark, o Dataproc é o serviço gerenciado de Spark que permite migrar o código praticamente sem mudanças, e o Workbench conectado ao cluster dá o ambiente interativo para a prova de conceito. A opção D (só um notebook n2-standard-4) é tentadora pelo custo, mas não fornece um ambiente Spark distribuído representativo da migração (embora hoje Dataproc Serverless a partir do Workbench também seja uma alternativa); instalar Spark manualmente em VM ou GKE (A, B) exige mais esforço. Dataproc, PySpark, Vertex AI Workbench, migração

You are collaborating on a model prototype with your team. You need to create a Vertex AI Workbench environment for the members of your team and also limit access to other employees in your project. What should you do? Criar uma service account dedicada com Vertex AI User, conceder Service Account User aos membros da equipe nessa conta e Notebook Viewer a eles restringe o acesso ao notebook apenas à equipe, seguindo least privilege. Usar a service account padrão do Compute Engine (B) amplia o acesso a outros funcionários, e A inverte os papéis (a service account não precisa de Notebook Viewer). IAM, service account, Vertex AI Workbench, least privilege

You are working on a prototype of a text classification model in a managed Vertex AI Workbench notebook. You want to quickly experiment with tokenizing text by using a Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) library. How should you add the library to your Jupyter kernel? Instalar com !pip install nltk --user em uma célula instala o pacote no ambiente do kernel em uso, que é o jeito rápido de experimentar. Instalar pelo terminal (A) pode instalar em outro ambiente Python que não o do kernel; imagem customizada (C) é exagero para um teste rápido. Vertex AI Workbench, pip, Jupyter kernel

You are developing a recommendation engine for an online clothing store. The historical customer transaction data is stored in BigQuery and Cloud Storage. You need to perform exploratory data analysis (EDA), preprocessing and model training. You plan to rerun these EDA, preprocessing, and training steps as you experiment with different types of algorithms. You want to minimize the cost and development effort of running these steps as you experiment. How should you configure the environment? Um managed notebook do Workbench tem integração nativa com BigQuery e Cloud Storage para navegar e consultar tabelas na interface do JupyterLab, minimizando esforço de configuração e gerenciamento. Clusters Dataproc (C/D) adicionam custo e complexidade desnecessários para esse volume de experimentação. Vertex AI Workbench, managed notebook, BigQuery, EDA

You need to design a customized deep neural network in Keras that will predict customer purchases based on their purchase history. You want to explore model performance using multiple model architectures, store training data, and be able to compare the evaluation metrics in the same dashboard. What should you do? Experiments no Kubeflow Pipelines (hoje Vertex AI Experiments) organizam várias execuções e permitem comparar métricas no mesmo dashboard. Jobs com nomes parecidos (C) não oferecem comparação estruturada, e AutoML Tables (A) não permite arquiteturas Keras customizadas. experiments, Kubeflow Pipelines, metric comparison

Your data science team needs to rapidly experiment with various features, model architectures, and hyperparameters. They need to track the accuracy metrics for various experiments and use an API to query the metrics over time. What should they use to track and report their experiments while minimizing manual effort? Kubeflow Pipelines registra métricas de cada execução automaticamente e permite consultá-las via API, com pouco esforço manual. Gravar métricas em BigQuery ou Cloud Monitoring (B, C) exige código extra. Hoje a escolha natural seria Vertex AI Experiments integrado a Vertex AI Pipelines. Kubeflow Pipelines, experiment tracking, métricas

Your data science team needs to rapidly experiment with various features, model architectures, and hyperparameters. They need to track the accuracy metrics for various experiments and use an API to query the metrics over time. What should they use to track and report their experiments while minimizing manual effort? Execuções em Vertex AI Pipelines registram parâmetros e métricas automaticamente no Vertex ML Metadata (MetadataStore), consultável via Vertex AI API, sem esforço manual. Gravar métricas em BigQuery ou Cloud Monitoring (B, C) exige código próprio. Hoje a resposta ideal seria Vertex AI Experiments, que usa esse mesmo metadata store. Vertex AI Pipelines, Vertex ML Metadata, experiment tracking

You created an ML pipeline with multiple input parameters. You want to investigate the tradeoffs between different parameter combinations. The parameter options are • Input dataset • Max tree depth of the boosted tree regressor • Optimizer learning rate You need to compare the pipeline performance of the different parameter combinations measured in F1 score, time to train, and model complexity. You want your approach to be reproducible, and track all pipeline runs on the same platform. What should you do? Vertex AI Experiments com várias execuções do mesmo Vertex AI pipeline parametrizado dá reprodutibilidade e compara métricas (F1, tempo, complexidade) em uma única plataforma. Otimização Bayesiana (B) busca o melhor valor em vez de comparar tradeoffs, e notebooks separados (C) não são reprodutíveis nem rastreados. Vertex AI Experiments, Vertex AI Pipelines, reproducibility

ou are training models in Vertex AI by using data that spans across multiple Google Cloud projects. You need to find, track, and compare the performance of the different versions of your models. Which Google Cloud services should you include in your ML workflow? Vertex AI Pipelines executa e registra os treinos, Vertex AI Experiments permite comparar desempenho entre runs e versões de modelo, e Vertex ML Metadata rastreia linhagem e artefatos, cobrindo encontrar, rastrear e comparar. Dataplex (C) é tentador por causa dos dados em vários projetos, mas é um serviço de governança/descoberta de dados, não de comparação de modelos; Feature Store (B) não ajuda a comparar versões de modelos. Vertex AI Experiments, Vertex ML Metadata, Vertex AI Pipelines, rastreamento

You have created a Vertex AI pipeline that automates custom model training. You want to add a pipeline component that enables your team to most easily collaborate when running different executions and comparing metrics both visually and programmatically. What should you do? Registrar métricas no Vertex ML Metadata e usar o Vertex AI Experiments permite comparar execuções do pipeline tanto na console (visualmente) quanto via SDK (programaticamente), com o Vertex AI TensorBoard para visualizações compartilhadas pela equipe. Soluções com BigQuery, Looker Studio ou pandas/Matplotlib (A, B, D) exigem construir e manter a infraestrutura de comparação manualmente. Vertex AI Experiments, Vertex ML Metadata, Vertex AI TensorBoard, colaboração

Your team is training a large number of ML models that use different algorithms, parameters, and datasets. Some models are trained in Vertex AI Pipelines, and some are trained on Vertex AI Workbench notebook instances. Your team wants to compare the performance of the models across both services. You want to minimize the effort required to store the parameters and metrics. What should you do? Um Vertex AI experiment aceita pipeline runs como experiment runs e, nos notebooks, o SDK (aiplatform.start run, log params, log metrics) registra parâmetros e métricas no mesmo experimento, permitindo comparar tudo em um só lugar com esforço mínimo. Migrar todos os modelos para Pipelines (C) é trabalhoso, e exportar para BigQuery ou usar a Metadata API diretamente (A, D) exige implementação própria. Vertex AI Experiments, Vertex AI SDK, Vertex AI Pipelines, métricas

You work on a team that builds state-of-the-art deep learning models by using the TensorFlow framework. Your team runs multiple ML experiments each week, which makes it difficult to track the experiment runs. You want a simple approach to effectively track, visualize, and debug ML experiment runs on Google Cloud while minimizing any overhead code. How should you proceed? Vertex AI Experiments registra parâmetros e métricas de cada run com pouco código, e o Vertex AI TensorBoard gerenciado oferece visualização e debug sem infraestrutura própria. As alternativas com Cloud Function e VM hospedando TensorBoard exigem código e operação manual, contrariando o requisito de mínimo overhead. Vertex AI Experiments, Vertex AI TensorBoard, experiment tracking

You are developing a model to predict whether a failure will occur in a critical machine part. You have a dataset consisting of a multivariate time series and labels indicating whether the machine part failed. You recently started experimenting with a few different preprocessing and modeling approaches in a Vertex AI Workbench notebook. You want to log data and track artifacts from each run. How should you set up your experiments? log time series metrics exige uma instância do Vertex AI TensorBoard associada ao experimento e serve para métricas ao longo de steps, como a curva de loss; os dados pré-processados devem ser rastreados como artefato com assign input artifact. O gabarito B usa log time series metrics para 'rastrear dados', o que não faz sentido, e não cria TensorBoard, sem o qual a função falha. Vertex AI Experiments, Vertex AI TensorBoard, log time series metrics, artifacts

You want to migrate a scikit-learn classifier model to TensorFlow. You plan to train the TensorFlow classifier model using the same training set that was used to train the scikit-learn model, and then compare the performances using a common test set. You want to use the Vertex AI Python SDK to manually log the evaluation metrics of each model and compare them based on their F1 scores and confusion matrices. How should you log the metrics? aiplatform.log classification metrics registra artefatos de classificação como confusion matrix e curva ROC, mas não aceita F1 score; métricas escalares como F1 vão em aiplatform.log metrics. O gabarito B é tentador pelo nome da função, mas ela não tem parâmetro para F1. Vertex AI Experiments, log metrics, log classification metrics, confusion matrix

You are developing an ML model in a Vertex AI Workbench notebook. You want to track artifacts and compare models during experimentation using different approaches. You need to rapidly and easily transition successful experiments to production as you iterate on your model implementation. What should you do? Inicializar o SDK com o experimento, registrar parâmetros e métricas e associar dataset e modelo como artefatos de entrada/saída de cada execução dá rastreabilidade de linhagem, e depois o experimento bem-sucedido vira um Vertex AI pipeline. Criar pipelines já na fase exploratória (C/D) desacelera a iteração. Vertex AI Experiments, ML Metadata, artifacts, Vertex AI Pipelines

Your organization wants to make its internal shuttle service route more efficient. The shuttles currently stop at all pick-up points across the city every 30 minutes between 7 am and 10 am. The development team has already built an application on Google Kubernetes Engine that requires users to confirm their presence and shuttle station one day in advance. What approach should you take? Como os usuários já confirmam presença e estação com um dia de antecedência, não há nada a prever: basta resolver um problema de otimização de rota (caminho mais curto com restrição de capacidade). Os modelos de regressão, classificação ou RL são tentadores, mas adicionam complexidade e erro desnecessários quando o dado já é conhecido. problem framing, otimização, quando não usar ML

our team needs to build a model that predicts whether images contain a driver's license, passport, or credit card. The data engineering team already built the pipeline and generated a dataset composed of 10,000 images with driver's licenses, 1,000 images with passports, and 1,000 images with credit cards. You now have to train a model with the following label map: [ ˜drivers license', ˜passport', ˜credit card']. Which loss function should you use? Com três classes mutuamente exclusivas e label map em formato categórico (one-hot), a perda adequada é categorical cross-entropy. Sparse categorical cross-entropy (D) é tentadora, mas é usada quando os rótulos são inteiros; binary cross-entropy serve para problemas binários ou multilabel. loss function, multiclass, cross-entropy

You are an ML engineer at a large grocery retailer with stores in multiple regions. You have been asked to create an inventory prediction model. Your model's features include region, location, historical demand, and seasonal popularity. You want the algorithm to learn from new inventory data on a daily basis. Which algorithms should you use to build the model? Previsão de inventário a partir de demanda histórica e sazonalidade é um problema de séries temporais, para o qual RNNs são a escolha entre as opções. Classificação (A) não prevê quantidade e CNN (D) é voltada a imagens; RL (B) é tentador pelo aprendizado diário, mas não é o tipo de problema. time series, RNN, forecasting

You are an ML engineer at a global shoe store. You manage the ML models for the company's website. You are asked to build a model that will recommend new products to the user based on their purchase behavior and similarity with other users. What should you do? Recomendar com base na similaridade com outros usuários é exatamente collaborative filtering. Knowledge-based filtering (B) usa regras ou atributos explícitos, não o comportamento de usuários semelhantes. recommendation, collaborative filtering

You are an ML engineer at a global car manufacture. You need to build an ML model to predict car sales in different cities around the world. Which features or feature crosses should you use to train city-specific relationships between car type and number of sales? Um único feature cross entre latitude binarizada, longitude binarizada e tipo de carro one-hot permite aprender relações específicas por cidade e tipo. Crosses separados (D) não capturam a combinação de latitude e longitude que define a cidade, e valores contínuos (B) não funcionam em crosses. feature cross, binning, one-hot encoding

Your team has been tasked with creating an ML solution in Google Cloud to classify support requests for one of your platforms. You analyzed the requirements and decided to use TensorFlow to build the classifier so that you have full control of the model's code, serving, and deployment. You will use Kubeflow pipelines for the ML platform. To save time, you want to build on existing resources and use managed services instead of building a completely new model. How should you build the classifier? Requisito de controle total do código em TensorFlow mais reaproveitar recursos existentes aponta para transfer learning sobre um modelo de classificação de texto já estabelecido. Natural Language API e AutoML (A, B) tiram o controle do código; usar o modelo as-is (D) não se adapta às categorias específicas de suporte. transfer learning, TensorFlow, classificação de texto

You are building a linear model with over 100 input features, all with values between –1 and 1. You suspect that many features are non-informative. You want to remove the non-informative features from your model while keeping the informative ones in their original form. Which technique should you use? L1 (Lasso) zera os coeficientes de features não informativas e mantém as demais no formato original, fazendo seleção de features embutida. PCA (A) é tentador, mas cria componentes combinados e perde o formato original das features. L1 regularization, feature selection, modelo linear

You are creating a deep neural network classification model using a dataset with categorical input values. Certain columns have a cardinality greater than 10,000 unique values. How should you encode these categorical values as input into the model? Para cardinalidade acima de 10 mil, hash buckets limitam a dimensionalidade sem manter um vocabulário enorme. Converter para inteiros (A) é tentador, mas impõe uma ordem artificial entre as categorias. feature hashing, alta cardinalidade, encoding

You need to train a natural language model to perform text classification on product descriptions that contain millions of examples and 100,000 unique words. You want to preprocess the words individually so that they can be fed into a recurrent neural network. What should you do? Word embeddings pré-treinados dão representações densas e semânticas para 100 mil palavras e funcionam bem com RNN. One-hot (A) gera vetores enormes e esparsos, e índices numéricos (D) impõem ordem sem significado. word embeddings, RNN, NLP

You work on the data science team for a multinational beverage company. You need to develop an ML model to predict the company’s profitability for a new line of naturally flavored bottled waters in different locations. You are provided with historical data that includes product types, product sales volumes, expenses, and profits for all regions. What should you use as the input and output for your model? Um feature cross de latitude com longitude, com binning, captura efeitos regionais que coordenadas cruas não capturam linearmente, e profit é o alvo direto do negócio. Prever revenue e expenses separadamente (B, D) complica o problema sem necessidade, e lat/long cruas (A) representam mal a localização. feature cross, binning, geolocalização

You work on the data science team for a multinational beverage company. You need to develop an ML model to predict the company’s profitability for a new line of naturally flavored bottled waters in different locations. You are provided with historical data that includes product types, product sales volumes, expenses, and profits for all regions. What should you use as the input and output for your model? Questão duplicada da anterior: o feature cross de latitude com longitude, com binning, representa a localização como regiões, e profit é o alvo direto. Usar lat/long como valores numéricos crus (A) é tentador, mas o modelo não aprende bem os efeitos regionais. feature cross, binning, geolocalização

You are an ML engineer at a manufacturing company. You need to build a model that identifies defects in products based on images of the product taken at the end of the assembly line. You want your model to preprocess the images with lower computation to quickly extract features of defects in products. Which approach should you use to build the model? CNNs são a arquitetura padrão para visão computacional: as convoluções extraem features locais (como defeitos) com compartilhamento de pesos, o que reduz o custo computacional. RNNs (C) são para sequências, e reinforcement learning e recommender systems não se aplicam a classificação de imagens. CNN, visão computacional, detecção de defeitos

You are an ML engineer at an ecommerce company and have been tasked with building a model that predicts how much inventory the logistics team should order each month. Which approach should you take? Demanda de estoque varia no tempo com sazonalidade e tendências, então um modelo de time series forecasting por item é o enquadramento correto. Regressão (B) é tentadora, mas prever 'estoque adicional' ignora a estrutura temporal e não se baseia nas vendas por item; clustering e classificação não produzem quantidades. time series forecasting, demand forecasting, enquadramento do problema

You work for a company that provides an anti-spam service that flags and hides spam posts on social media platforms. Your company currently uses a list of 200,000 keywords to identify suspected spam posts. If a post contains more than a few of these keywords, the post is identified as spam. You want to start using machine learning to flag spam posts for human review. What is the main advantage of implementing machine learning for this business case? A vantagem de ML sobre a lista fixa de palavras-chave é generalizar e identificar novos padrões e frases problemáticas que não estão na lista. As demais opções descrevem ganhos que continuam presos ao paradigma de palavras-chave. ML vs regras, generalização, spam

You work for a company that is developing a new video streaming platform. You have been asked to create a recommendation system that will suggest the next video for a user to watch. After a review by an AI Ethics team, you are approved to start development. Each video asset in your company’s catalog has useful metadata (e.g., content type, release date, country), but you do not have any historical user event data. How should you build the recommendation system for the first version of the product? Sem dados de eventos de usuário, a recomendação é lançar com heurísticas simples baseadas nos metadados e coletar dados para treinar um modelo depois (regra 1 do Rules of ML). Usar MovieLens (C) é tentador, mas o modelo treinado em outro catálogo não transfere; o autoencoder (D) é complexo sem sinal de preferência dos usuários. cold start, heurísticas, Rules of ML

You are an ML engineer on an agricultural research team working on a crop disease detection tool to detect leaf rust spots in images of crops to determine the presence of a disease. These spots, which can vary in shape and size, are correlated to the severity of the disease. You want to develop a solution that predicts the presence and severity of the disease with high accuracy. What should you do? Como forma e tamanho das manchas se correlacionam com a severidade, a segmentação de imagem, que delimita os contornos pixel a pixel, dá a informação necessária para prever presença e severidade. Object detection (A) é tentador, mas bounding boxes não capturam a forma e a área exata; classificação (D) só indica presença. image segmentation, visão computacional, object detection

You work on a team in a data center that is responsible for server maintenance. Your management team wants you to build a predictive maintenance solution that uses monitoring data to detect potential server failures. Incident data has not been labeled yet. What should you do first? Sem rótulos, o primeiro passo prático é criar rótulos com uma heurística simples (z-score) sobre os dados históricos e então treinar um modelo de detecção de anomalias com eles. A opção A (prever o desempenho por série temporal e alertar em desvios) é tentadora e tem a maioria dos votos, mas não aproveita os dados de incidentes e funciona mais como monitoramento do que como previsão de falhas; contratar analistas (D) é caro e lento. predictive maintenance, heurística de rotulagem, anomaly detection

You are working on a binary classification ML algorithm that detects whether an image of a classified scanned document contains a company’s logo. In the dataset, 96% of examples don’t have the logo, so the dataset is very skewed. Which metric would give you the most confidence in your model? Com 96% de negativos, accuracy engana e olhar só precision ou só recall dá uma visão parcial; o F1 score equilibra os dois e é a métrica mais confiável aqui. RMSE (C) é métrica de regressão. F1 score, imbalanced data, precision, recall

You are developing a classification model to support predictions for your company’s various products. The dataset you were given for model development has class imbalance You need to minimize false positives and false negatives What evaluation metric should you use to properly train the model? Minimizar falsos positivos e falsos negativos ao mesmo tempo pede o F1 score, a média harmônica de precision e recall. Accuracy (C) engana com classes desbalanceadas, e precision ou recall sozinhos otimizam só um dos tipos de erro. F1 score, class imbalance, evaluation metrics

You work for a retail company. You have been asked to develop a model to predict whether a customer will purchase a product on a given day. Your team has processed the company’s sales data, and created a table with the following rows: • Customer id • Product id • Date • Days since last purchase (measured in days) • Average purchase frequency (measured in 1/days) • Purchase (binary class, if customer purchased product on the Date) You need to interpret your model’s results for each individual prediction. What should you do? AutoML tabular implantado em endpoint com feature attributions habilitadas permite chamar o método explain e obter a contribuição de cada feature por predição individual, com mínimo esforço. Inspecionar regras de partição das árvores (A) é inviável em ensembles, e coeficientes de regressão logística (C) dão importância global, não por predição, e dependem da escala das features. Vertex Explainable AI, feature attributions, AutoML, explain

You work as an analyst at a large banking firm. You are developing a robust scalable ML pipeline to tram several regression and classification models. Your primary focus for the pipeline is model interpretability. You want to productionize the pipeline as quickly as possible. What should you do? O Tabular Workflow for TabNet é um pipeline gerenciado no Vertex AI Pipelines cujo modelo baseado em atenção é intrinsecamente interpretável (feature masks), atendendo regressão e classificação com rápida produtização. Wide & Deep (A) é menos interpretável, e GKE ou Composer com modelos customizados (B, D) exigem muito mais esforço de construção. Tabular Workflows, TabNet, interpretabilidade, Vertex AI Pipelines

You are developing a model to identify traffic signs in images extracted from videos taken from the dashboard of a vehicle. You work at an ecommerce startup. You need to create a customer churn prediction model. Your company’s recent sales records are stored in a BigQuery table. You work at an ecommerce startup. You need to create a customer churn prediction model. Your company’s recent sales records are stored in a BigQuery table. Your team is working on an NLP research project to predict political affiliation of authors based on articles they have written. You are experimenting with a built-in distributed XGBoost model in Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks. You use BigQuery to split your data into training and validation sets using the following queries: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ‘myproject.mydataset.training‘ AS (SELECT FROM ‘myproject.mydataset.mytable‘ WHERE RAND() <= 0.8); CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ‘myproject.mydataset.validation‘ AS (SELECT FROM ‘myproject.mydataset.mytable‘ WHERE RAND() <= 0.2); After training the model, you achieve an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC ROC) value of 0.8, but after deploying the model to production, you notice that your model performance has dropped to an AUC ROC value of 0.65. You are training an LSTM-based model on AI Platform to summarize text using the following job submission script: gcloud ai-platform jobs submit training $JOB NAME \ --package-path $TRAINER PACKAGE PATH \ --module-name $MAIN TRAINER MODULE \ --job-dir $JOB DIR \ --region $REGION \ --scale-tier basic \ -- \ --epochs 20 \ --batch size=32 \ --learning rate=0.001 \ You want to ensure that training time is minimized without significantly compromising the accuracy of your model. Your team is building a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based architecture from scratch. You are training an object detection machine learning model on a dataset that consists of three million X-ray images, each roughly 2 GB in size. You recently developed a deep learning model using Keras, and now you are experimenting with different training strategies. First, you trained the model using a single GPU, but the training process was too slow. Next, you distributed the training across 4 GPUs using tf.distribute.MirroredStrategy (with no other changes), but you did not observe a decrease in training time. What should you do? Com MirroredStrategy, o batch global é dividido entre as réplicas; sem aumentar o batch size, cada GPU processa um lote pequeno e o overhead de sincronização anula o ganho. O correto é escalar o batch size proporcionalmente ao número de GPUs. Distribuir o dataset manualmente (A) é tentador, mas o Keras fit já faz isso automaticamente. MirroredStrategy, batch size, treino distribuído

You work for a biotech startup that is experimenting with deep learning ML models based on properties of biological organisms. What hardware should you choose for your models? Custom TensorFlow ops escritas em C++ rodam em CPU sem trabalho adicional, enquanto GPUs exigiriam kernels CUDA e TPUs não suportam custom ops; por isso o cluster só de CPUs é o adequado. As opções com GPUs A100/V100 (A, B) são tentadoras pelo tamanho do modelo e do batch, mas não executariam as ops customizadas. custom ops, CPU, escolha de hardware

You are building a TensorFlow model for a financial institution that predicts the impact of consumer spending on inflation globally. Como o treino tem checkpoints frequentes, ele tolera interrupções, e uma TPU preemptible custa bem menos que a não-preemptible. A TPU não-preemptible (C) é tentadora pela estabilidade, mas custa mais; GPUs P100 seriam mais lentas e o custo total maior para um treino longo. TPU, preemptible, checkpointing

You are training an object detection model using a Cloud TPU v2. Training time is taking longer than expected. Based on this simplified trace obtained with a Cloud TPU profile, what action should you take to decrease training time in a cost-efficient way? Migrar para TPU v3 ou GPUs (A, B) é tentador, mas custa mais e não resolve um gargalo de entrada. Cloud TPU profiler, tf.data, prefetch

You are training an object detection machine learning model on a dataset that consists of three million X-ray images, each roughly 2 GB in size. You are training an ML model on a large dataset. You are using a TPU to accelerate the training process. You notice that the training process is taking longer than expected.
