Mudar learning rate ou epochs (A, B, C) não altera a ocupação do hardware. TPU, batch size, utilization

You developed a Transformer model in TensorFlow to translate text. Your training data includes millions of documents in a Cloud Storage bucket. What should you do? Um custom training job do Vertex AI com GPUs no worker pool de workers e tf.distribute.MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy distribui o Transformer em várias máquinas com mudança mínima de código e o cluster é gerenciado pelo Vertex AI. Reduction Server (B) acrescenta configuração de pools extras, TPU VMs (C) exigem gerenciar a infraestrutura de TPU, e MirroredStrategy em um único pool (D) fica limitado a uma máquina. MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy, custom training, treino distribuído, GPU

A TensorFlow machine learning model on Compute Engine virtual machines (n2- standard-32) takes two days to complete training. GPUs aceleram o treino e suportam modelos com custom TensorFlow operations que precisam rodar parcialmente em CPU, reduzindo o tempo de forma custo-efetiva. TPUs (D) são tentadoras pela performance, mas não suportam bem custom ops que exigem CPU; trocar o tipo de VM de CPU (A, B) não reduz significativamente dois dias de treino. GPU, custom ops, TPU, tempo de treino

You are training a custom language model for your company using a large dataset. You plan to use the Reduction Server strategy on Vertex AI. O Reduction Server do Vertex AI funciona com workers em GPU (all-reduce via NCCL), e os reducers do terceiro worker pool usam o container reductionserver sem aceleradores, em máquinas com alta largura de banda de rede. O gabarito D está errado porque Reduction Server não é suportado com TPUs, e colocar GPUs nos reducers (A) desperdiça custo, já que eles apenas agregam gradientes. Reduction Server, treino distribuído, GPU, worker pools

You are pre-training a large language model on Google Cloud. This model includes custom TensorFlow operations in the training loop. Entre as GPUs, 8 nós a2-megagpu-16g (16 A100 cada) com MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy oferecem as mesmas 128 GPUs da opção D com menos nós e menos comunicação entre máquinas, reduzindo tempo e custo; máquinas apenas com CPU (C) seriam lentas demais para pré-treinar um LLM. GPU, TPU, custom ops, MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy

CPR com a interface Predictor encapsula pré e pós-processamento em Python junto ao modelo XGBoost, e o endpoint gerenciado tira a manutenção de infraestrutura. FastAPI (A, B) exige escrever o servidor, e reescrever o processamento em Go (D) causa retrabalho e risco de skew. custom prediction routine, XGBoost, Vertex AI endpoint

You work for a social media company. You want to create a no-code image classification model for an iOS mobile application to identify fashion accessories. Para iOS, exportar o modelo AutoML Edge como Core ML roda nativo no dispositivo, com latência mínima e sem custo de endpoint. TFLite (C) também funciona no iOS, mas Core ML é o formato nativo e mais otimizado para a plataforma. Endpoints online ou batch (A, D) adicionam latência de rede e custo. AutoML Edge, Core ML, on-device

Your company manages an ecommerce website. You developed an ML model that recommends additional products to users in near real time based on items currently in the user’s cart. The workflow will include the following processes: 1. The website will send a Pub/Sub message with the relevant data and then receive a message with the prediction from Pub/Sub 2. Predictions will be stored in BigQuery 3. The model will be stored in a Cloud Storage bucket and will be updated frequently You want to minimize prediction latency and the effort required to update the model. How should you reconfigure the architecture? Um job de Dataflow streaming lendo do Pub/Sub com RunInference carrega o modelo dentro do worker (baixa latência, sem chamada de rede extra), e WatchFilePattern detecta automaticamente novas versões do modelo no Cloud Storage, atualizando-o sem redeploy; o resultado pode ser gravado no BigQuery e no Pub/Sub. Chamar um endpoint a partir de um DoFn (C) adiciona latência de rede e exige redeploy para atualizar o modelo; Cloud Functions (A) recarregam o modelo e escalam mal. You recently trained a XGBoost model that you plan to deploy to production for online inference. Uma custom prediction routine (CPR) baseada no XGBoost Predictor do Vertex AI SDK permite incluir o pré-processamento no handler, usando uma imagem pré-construída, com o modelo armazenado no Cloud Storage e carregado como artefato, o que facilita trocar o modelo sem rebuild. Empacotar o modelo dentro da imagem (C) obriga a reconstruir o container a cada versão, e apps Flask próprios (A, B) exigem mais esforço. custom prediction routine, XGBoost, Vertex AI Endpoints, pré-processamento

You work for a retail company that is using a regression model built with BigQuery ML to predict product sales. This model is being used to serve online predictions. How should you deploy the model? Importar o novo modelo como nova versão do mesmo modelo no Model Registry e implantá-lo no mesmo endpoint com traffic splitting 95/5 faz um canary sem mudar a interface para os usuários atuais e futuros. A opção B é parecida, mas não registra como versão do mesmo modelo, perdendo o versionamento; endpoints separados (C, D) exigiriam que os clientes mudassem a forma de chamar. You work at a mobile gaming startup that creates online multiplayer games. You want your serving solution to provide immediate classifications after a completed game session to avoid further loss of revenue. What should you do? Classificações imediatas após cada sessão exigem online prediction, e um Vertex AI endpoint gerenciado com o modelo do Model Registry é a solução de serving recomendada, escalável e de baixa latência. Batch prediction (A) não é imediata, e Cloud Functions ou VM carregando o modelo a cada requisição (B, C) aumentam latência e esforço operacional. online prediction, Vertex AI Endpoints, Model Registry

Your work for a textile manufacturing company. Your company has hundreds of machines, and each machine has many sensors. Your team used the sensory data to build hundreds of ML models that detect machine anomalies. Models are retrained daily, and you need to deploy these models in a cost-effective way. The models must operate 24/7 without downtime and make sub millisecond predictions. What should you do? Um pipeline Dataflow streaming com RunInference executa a inferência dentro dos workers, evitando chamadas de rede a um endpoint (necessário para latência sub-milissegundo), e o automatic model refresh troca os modelos retreinados diariamente sem downtime. Endpoints Vertex AI para centenas de modelos seriam caros e adicionariam latência de rede; pipelines batch não atendem operação 24/7 em tempo real. Dataflow, RunInference, model refresh, streaming

You recently used BigQuery ML to train an AutoML regression model. You shared results with your team and received positive feedback. You need to deploy your model for online prediction as quickly as possible. What should you do? Um modelo BigQuery ML já treinado pode ser registrado no Vertex AI Model Registry com ALTER MODEL ... SET OPTIONS (vertex ai model id=...), sem retreinar nem exportar, e depois implantado em um endpoint — o caminho mais rápido. Exportar para Cloud Storage e importar (D) funciona, mas adiciona etapas manuais; retreinar (A/B) desperdiça tempo. BigQuery ML, Vertex AI Model Registry, ALTER MODEL, online prediction

You recently used BigQuery ML to train an AutoML regression model. You shared results with your team and received positive feedback. You need to deploy your model for online prediction as quickly as possible. What should you do? Mesma questão da 246: ALTER MODEL ... O gabarito D (export para Cloud Storage e import) também funciona, mas tem mais passos manuais, então não é o 'mais rápido possível'; a comunidade está dividida (C ~50%, D ~44%). You trained a model packaged it with a custom Docker container for serving, and deployed it to Vertex AI Model Registry. You recently trained an XGBoost model on tabular data. You plan to expose the model for internal use as an HTTP microservice. After deployment, you expect a small number of incoming requests. You have developed an application that uses a chain of multiple scikit-learn models to predict the optimal price for your company’s products. The workflow logic is shown in the diagram. You work for an organization that operates a streaming music service. You have a custom production model that is serving a “next song” recommendation based on a user's recent listening history. You now want to test the new model in production while minimizing complexity. What should you do? Criar outro endpoint e um serviço para dividir tráfego (A) faz manualmente o que o endpoint já oferece. traffic splitting, A/B testing, Vertex AI endpoint

You developed an ML model with AI Platform, and you want to move it to production. You serve a few thousand queries per second and are experiencing latency issues. Incoming requests are served by a load balancer that distributes them across multiple Kubeflow CPU-only pods running on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Your goal is to improve the serving latency without changing the underlying infrastructure. What should you do? Recompilar o TensorFlow Serving com otimizações de CPU (AVX etc.) e fixar uma plataforma mínima de CPU no GKE reduz a latência sem mudar a infraestrutura. Aumentar muito max batch size (A) é tentador, mas melhora throughput à custa de latência, pois as requisições esperam o lote encher. TensorFlow Serving, latency, CPU optimization, GKE

You work for an online travel agency that also sells advertising placements on its website to other companies. You have been asked to predict the most relevant web banner that a user should see next. Security is important to your company. The model latency requirements are 300ms@p99, the inventory is thousands of web banners, and your exploratory analysis has shown that navigation context is a good predictor. You want to Implement the simplest solution. How should you configure the prediction pipeline? Como o contexto de navegação é o principal preditor, é preciso um banco de baixa latência para gravar e ler esse contexto por usuário, e o Bigtable atende isso dentro do p99 de 300 ms; o gateway no App Engine protege o endpoint. A opção B é tentadora por ser mais simples, mas não tem onde armazenar o contexto de navegação; a D com GKE e Memorystore é complexa demais. online serving, Bigtable, latency, App Engine

You have deployed a model on Vertex AI for real-time inference. During an online prediction request, you get an “Out of Memory” error. What should you do? Out of Memory em uma requisição online normalmente indica payload grande demais; reenviar com menos instâncias por request resolve. Batch prediction (A) muda o padrão de uso sem necessidade, e quota (D) gera erro 429, não OOM. online prediction, Out of Memory, Vertex AI Prediction

You work for an online travel agency that also sells advertising placements on its website to other companies. You have been asked to predict the most relevant web banner that a user should see next. Security is important to your company. The model latency requirements are 300ms@p99, the inventory is thousands of web banners, and your exploratory analysis has shown that navigation context is a good predictor. You want to Implement the simplest solution. How should you configure the prediction pipeline? É preciso guardar e ler o contexto de navegação do usuário, e um gateway no App Engine protege o endpoint do modelo (segurança). Firestore é a opção gerenciada mais simples para essa leitura e escrita dentro de 300 ms. Bigtable (C) é tentador pela baixa latência, mas é dimensionado para volumes muito maiores e é mais complexo do que o 'simplest solution' pede. serving architecture, Firestore, latência

You work for a toy manufacturer that has been experiencing a large increase in demand. You need to build an ML model to reduce the amount of time spent by quality control inspectors checking for product defects. Faster defect detection is a priority. The factory does not have reliable Wi-Fi. Your company wants to implement the new ML model as soon as possible. Which model should you use? Sem Wi-Fi confiável o modelo precisa rodar no dispositivo (Edge), e como a prioridade é detecção rápida, o modelo mobile-low-latency-1 é o indicado. O mobile-high-accuracy-1 (A) é tentador, mas troca latência por acurácia; o AutoML Vision em nuvem (C) depende de conectividade. AutoML Edge, baixa latência, edge deployment

You are working on a system log anomaly detection model for a cybersecurity organization. You have developed the model using TensorFlow, and you plan to use it for real-time prediction. You need to create a Dataflow pipeline to ingest data via Pub/Sub and write the results to BigQuery. You want to minimize the serving latency as much as possible. What should you do? Carregar o modelo diretamente no job Dataflow (por exemplo, via RunInference) elimina a chamada de rede a um serviço externo, o que dá a menor latência possível de serving. O gabarito C (endpoint do Vertex AI) é tentador por ser gerenciado, mas cada predição adiciona um round-trip HTTP; Cloud Run e GKE têm o mesmo problema. Esta é a resposta do conjunto de questões de exemplo do Google. Dataflow, RunInference, latência

You have trained a DNN regressor with TensorFlow to predict housing prices using a set of predictive features. Your default precision is tf.float64, and you use a standard TensorFlow estimator: Your model performs well, but just before deploying it to production, you discover that your current serving latency is 10ms @ 90 percentile and you currently serve on CPUs. Your production requirements expect a model latency of 8ms @ 90 percentile. You're willing to accept a small decrease in performance in order to reach the latency requirement. Therefore your plan is to improve latency while evaluating how much the model's prediction decreases. What should you first try to quickly lower the serving latency? Quantização para float16 (o modelo está em float64) reduz o custo computacional e a latência de inferência rapidamente, com pequena perda de qualidade, exatamente o trade-off aceito. Trocar para GPU (A) é tentador, mas é mais caro e nem sempre reduz latência para modelos pequenos com requisições individuais; dropout não afeta a inferência (C, D). quantização, latência, float16

You are an ML engineer at a retail company. You have built a model that predicts a coupon to offer an ecommerce customer at checkout based on the items in their cart. When a customer goes to checkout, your serving pipeline, which is hosted on Google Cloud, joins the customer's existing cart with a row in a BigQuery table that contains the customers' historic purchase behavior and uses that as the model's input. The web team is reporting that your model is returning predictions too slowly to load the coupon offer with the rest of the web page. How should you speed up your model's predictions? O gargalo é a consulta ao BigQuery no caminho de serving: o BigQuery é um data warehouse analítico, sem latência de milissegundos. Mover o histórico para um banco de baixa latência (Bigtable, Memorystore ou Feature Store online serving) é a prática recomendada. A materialized view (D) reduz o custo da query, mas continua sujeita à latência do BigQuery, por isso a escolha é B. online serving, low latency, Bigtable, Feature Store

You work for a small company that has deployed an ML model with autoscaling on Vertex AI to serve online predictions in a production environment. The current model receives about 20 prediction requests per hour with an average response time of one second. You have retrained the same model on a new batch of data, and now you are canary testing it, sending ~10% of production traffic to the new model. During this canary test, you notice that prediction requests for your new model are taking between 30 and 180 seconds to complete. What should you do? Com tráfego baixíssimo, o autoscaling deixa o modelo novo sem nós aquecidos e cada requisição sofre cold start; manter um nó sempre disponível elimina a latência de 30 a 180 s. Comparar o código (C) é tentador, mas o modelo é o mesmo retreinado, então o problema é de infraestrutura e não de código. autoscaling, cold start, canary

You need to deploy a scikit-leam classification model to production. The model must be able to serve requests 24/7, and you expect millions of requests per second to the production application from 8 am to 7 pm. You need to minimize the cost of deployment. What should you do? scikit-learn não se beneficia de GPU no serving, então GPUs (C, D) só aumentam custo; e com milhões de requisições por segundo em horário de pico é preciso autoscaling até muitas réplicas (max 100), que voltam ao mínimo fora do pico. Max replicas = 1 (A) não aguenta a carga. autoscaling, replica count, scikit-learn, cost

You need to deploy a scikit-leam classification model to production. The model must be able to serve requests 24/7, and you expect millions of requests per second to the production application from 8 am to 7 pm. You need to minimize the cost of deployment. What should you do? Questão duplicada da anterior. Os prebuilt containers de scikit-learn não usam GPU, então GPU por réplica (D) só aumenta custo sem ganho; a resposta correta é autoscaling com max 100 réplicas em CPU (B). O gabarito D contraria o requisito de minimizar custo. autoscaling, scikit-learn, GPU, cost

You recently deployed a scikit-learn model to a Vertex AI endpoint. You are now testing the model on live production traffic. While monitoring the endpoint, you discover twice as many requests per hour than expected throughout the day. You want the endpoint to efficiently scale when the demand increases in the future to prevent users from experiencing high latency. What should you do? Definir minReplicaCount pelo tráfego base garante capacidade aquecida e deixa o autoscaling cuidar dos picos sem latência de cold start. Aumentar o target de utilização (C) faz escalar mais tarde, o que piora a latência, e GPU para scikit-learn (D) não ajuda. autoscaling, minReplicaCount, Vertex AI endpoint

You have built a custom model that performs several memory-intensive preprocessing tasks before it makes a prediction. You deployed the model to a Vertex AI endpoint, and validated that results were received in a reasonable amount of time. After routing user traffic to the endpoint, you discover that the endpoint does not autoscale as expected when receiving multiple requests. What should you do? O autoscaling do Vertex AI Endpoints se baseia na utilização de CPU/GPU; como o gargalo é memória, a CPU não atinge o alvo e novas réplicas não são criadas, então reduzir o CPU utilization target faz o escalonamento ocorrer antes. Uma máquina com mais memória (A) é tentadora, mas não resolve o fato de o autoscaling não ser acionado; aumentar o target (C) piora o problema. autoscaling, Vertex AI Endpoints, CPU utilization target

You have deployed a scikit-team model to a Vertex AI endpoint using a custom model server. You enabled autoscaling: however, the deployed model fails to scale beyond one replica, which led to dropped requests. You notice that CPU utilization remains low even during periods of high load. What should you do? Se a CPU fica baixa mesmo sob alta carga, o model server customizado está limitado pelo número de workers e não consegue usar a CPU disponível; aumentar os workers eleva o uso de CPU, permitindo atender mais requisições e acionar o autoscaling. Aumentar minReplicaCount (D) é tentador, mas só mascara o problema com custo fixo maior, e GPU (A) não ajuda um modelo scikit-learn. autoscaling, model server, workers, Vertex AI Endpoints

You work for an online grocery store. You recently developed a custom ML model that recommends a recipe when a user arrives at the website. You chose the machine type on the Vertex AI endpoint to optimize costs by using the queries per second (QPS) that the model can serve, and you deployed it on a single machine with 8 vCPUs and no accelerators. A holiday season is approaching and you anticipate four times more traffic during this time than the typical daily traffic. You need to ensure that the model can scale efficiently to the increased demand. What should you do? Autoscaling no endpoint com o mesmo machine type (já dimensionado por QPS) adiciona réplicas conforme o uso de vCPU, escalando de forma eficiente para o pico e voltando depois. Trocar para 32 vCPUs ou GPU aumenta custo permanentemente, e escalar manualmente após alertas é reativo. autoscaling, Vertex AI endpoint, QPS

You recently deployed a model to a Vertex AI endpoint and set up online serving in Vertex AI Feature Store. You have configured a daily batch ingestion job to update your featurestore. During the batch ingestion jobs, you discover that CPU utilization is high in your featurestore’s online serving nodes and that feature retrieval latency is high. You need to improve online serving performance during the daily batch ingestion. What should you do? Habilitar autoscaling dos nós de online serving do featurestore faz o Vertex AI adicionar nós quando a CPU sobe durante a ingestão batch, mantendo a latência baixa sem intervenção manual. Agendar aumento de nós (A) funciona, mas é manual e frágil; aumentar worker count (D) piora a carga nos nós. Vertex AI Feature Store, online serving nodes, autoscaling, batch ingestion

You work for a large bank that serves customers through an application hosted in Google Cloud that is running in the US and Singapore. You have developed a PyTorch model to classify transactions as potentially fraudulent or not. The model is a three-layer perceptron that uses both numerical and categorical features as input, and hashing happens within the model. You deployed the model to the us-central1 region on nl-highcpu-16 machines, and predictions are served in real time. The model's current median response latency is 40 ms. You want to reduce latency, especially in Singapore, where some customers are experiencing the longest delays. What should you do? Implantar em private endpoints em us-central1 e asia-southeast1 reduz a latência de rede para Singapura e elimina overhead do endpoint público, e a aplicação escolhe o endpoint mais próximo. D é tentadora por também aproximar o modelo, mas com endpoint público não aproveita o caminho de menor latência dos private endpoints; GPU ou mais CPU (A/B) não resolvem a distância geográfica de um MLP pequeno. private endpoint, latência, multi-region

You are building an ML model to detect anomalies in real-time sensor data. You will use Pub/Sub to handle incoming requests. You want to store the results for analytics and visualization. How should you configure the pipeline? Pub/Sub alimenta um job de streaming no Dataflow, que chama o modelo servido (hoje em Vertex AI) e grava os resultados no BigQuery para analytics e visualização. As alternativas com BigQuery como primeiro passo ou Cloud Storage/Cloud Functions como destino não formam um pipeline de streaming adequado para análise. Pub/Sub, Dataflow, BigQuery, streaming

You have trained a model on a dataset that required computationally expensive preprocessing operations. You need to execute the same preprocessing at prediction time. You deployed the model on AI Platform for high-throughput online prediction. Which architecture should you use? Dataflow em streaming lê o Pub/Sub e aplica o pré-processamento pesado em escala antes de chamar o endpoint, garantindo consistência entre treino e serving com alto throughput. Cloud Functions (D) é tentador, mas não é adequado para pré-processamento computacionalmente caro em alto volume. Dataflow, Pub/Sub, preprocessing, training-serving skew

You are developing a Kubeflow pipeline on Google Kubernetes Engine. The first step in the pipeline is to issue a query against BigQuery. You plan to use the results of that query as the input to the next step in your pipeline. You want to achieve this in the easiest way possible. What should you do? Reutilizar o componente pronto de BigQuery do Kubeflow Pipelines é a forma mais fácil. Escrever um componente ou script customizado (B, C) funciona, mas exige mais código e manutenção. Kubeflow Pipelines, prebuilt components, BigQuery

You work for a global footwear retailer and need to predict when an item will be out of stock based on historical inventory data Customer behavior is highly dynamic since footwear demand is influenced by many different factors. You want to serve models that are trained on all available data, but track your performance on specific subsets of data before pushing to production. What is the most streamlined and reliable way to perform this validation? Validar a performance em subconjuntos específicos (slices) antes do push é o papel do TFX ModelValidator, hoje o componente Evaluator com TFMA, que bloqueia modelos fora dos limites. Usar a última semana como validação (C) é tentador por causa da dinâmica temporal, mas não avalia slices e conflita com treinar em todos os dados. TFX, TFMA, model validation

You work on an operations team at an international company that manages a large fleet of on-premises servers located in few data centers around the world. Your team collects monitoring data from the servers, including CPU/memory consumption. When an incident occurs on a server, your team is responsible for fixing it. Incident data has not been properly labeled yet. Your management team wants you to build a predictive maintenance solution that uses monitoring data from the VMs to detect potential failures and then alerts the service desk team. What should you do first? Sem rótulos, o primeiro passo é uma heurística simples (z-score) e validar seu valor em produção antes de investir em ML, seguindo a regra 'comece sem ML'. Treinar um modelo sobre rótulos heurísticos (B) é tentador, mas só replicaria a heurística antes de saber se ela é útil. heurística, predictive maintenance, rules of ML

You are developing an ML model that uses sliced frames from video feed and creates bounding boxes around specific objects. You want to automate the following steps in your training pipeline: ingestion and preprocessing of data in Cloud Storage, followed by training and hyperparameter tuning of the object model using Vertex AI jobs, and finally deploying the model to an endpoint. You want to orchestrate the entire pipeline with minimal cluster management. What approach should you use? Vertex AI Pipelines é serverless (sem cluster para gerenciar), e o Kubeflow Pipelines SDK é o recomendado quando não se usa TFX e há componentes de Vertex AI jobs. TFX SDK (B) é indicado para TensorFlow com dados estruturados ou volumes muito grandes; Kubeflow em GKE e Composer (A, D) exigem gerenciar infraestrutura. Vertex AI Pipelines, Kubeflow Pipelines SDK, orquestração

One of your models is trained using data provided by a third-party data broker. The data broker does not reliably notify you of formatting changes in the data. You want to make your model training pipeline more robust to issues like this. What should you do? TensorFlow Data Validation infere o schema e detecta anomalias como mudanças de formato, tipos ou valores fora do domínio, tornando o pipeline robusto a mudanças do fornecedor. Substituir valores por 0 com TF Transform (B) é tentador, mas mascara o problema silenciosamente em vez de sinalizá-lo; funções customizadas (C, D) dão mais trabalho e só pegam erros conhecidos. TFDV, schema, validação de dados

You are an ML engineer responsible for designing and implementing training pipelines for ML models. You need to create an end-to-end training pipeline for a TensorFlow model. The TensorFlow model will be trained on several terabytes of structured data. You need the pipeline to include data quality checks before training and model quality checks after training but prior to deployment. You want to minimize development time and the need for infrastructure maintenance. How should you build and orchestrate your training pipeline? TFX tem componentes padrão para validação de dados (ExampleValidator/TFDV) e de modelo (Evaluator/TFMA), feitos para modelos TensorFlow em grande escala, e o Vertex AI Pipelines é serverless, eliminando manutenção. KFP com componentes Google (A) é tentador, mas exigiria construir as checagens de qualidade; GKE (C, D) traz manutenção de infraestrutura. TFX, Vertex AI Pipelines, validação de modelo

You have been asked to productionize a proof-of-concept ML model built using Keras. The model was trained in a Jupyter notebook on a data scientist’s local machine. The notebook contains a cell that performs data validation and a cell that performs model analysis. You need to orchestrate the steps contained in the notebook and automate the execution of these steps for weekly retraining. You expect much more training data in the future. You want your solution to take advantage of managed services while minimizing cost. What should you do? TFX tem componentes padrão de validação de dados e análise de modelo que substituem as células do notebook, e o Vertex AI Pipelines executa serverless, escalando com mais dados e cobrando só pelo uso. Cloud Composer (D) é tentador para orquestração, mas tem custo fixo de ambiente e exige reescrever tudo em BashOperators; agendar um notebook grande (A) não escala e é caro. TFX, Vertex AI Pipelines, retreino agendado

You are the Director of Data Science at a large company, and your Data Science team has recently begun using the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to orchestrate their training pipelines. Your team is struggling to integrate their custom Python code into the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK. How should you instruct them to proceed in order to quickly integrate their code with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK? func to container op transforma uma função Python em componente de pipeline de forma rápida, sem construir imagens manualmente. Empacotar em Docker e usar load component from file (C) funciona, mas é mais trabalhoso; Dataproc e Cloud Functions adicionam complexidade desnecessária. Kubeflow Pipelines, lightweight components, Python

You have built a model that is trained on data stored in Parquet files. You access the data through a Hive table hosted on Google Cloud. You preprocessed these data with PySpark and exported it as a CSV file into Cloud Storage. After preprocessing, you execute additional steps to train and evaluate your model. You want to parametrize this model training in Kubeflow Pipelines. What should you do? Adicionar um passo no pipeline que cria um cluster Dataproc efêmero, executa a transformação PySpark e grava em Cloud Storage parametriza o processo usando serviço gerenciado para Spark. Containerizar o PySpark (B) é tentador, mas rodar Spark dentro de um único container não escala; manter Spark no GKE (D) exige administração. Kubeflow Pipelines, Dataproc, PySpark

While running a model training pipeline on Vertex Al, you discover that the evaluation step is failing because of an out-of-memory error. You are currently using TensorFlow Model Analysis (TFMA) with a standard Evaluator TensorFlow Extended (TFX) pipeline component for the evaluation step. You want to stabilize the pipeline without downgrading the evaluation quality while minimizing infrastructure overhead. What should you do? O Evaluator do TFX roda sobre Apache Beam; passar --runner=DataflowRunner em beam pipeline args distribui a avaliação em workers gerenciados e resolve o OOM sem infraestrutura extra. Limitar métricas (D) reduz a qualidade da avaliação, e VMs ou GKE próprios (B, C) aumentam o overhead. TFX Evaluator, TFMA, Dataflow, Apache Beam

You have created a Vertex AI pipeline that includes two steps. The first step preprocesses 10 TB data completes in about 1 hour, and saves the result in a Cloud Storage bucket. The second step uses the processed data to train a model. You need to update the model’s code to allow you to test different algorithms. You want to reduce pipeline execution time and cost while also minimizing pipeline changes. What should you do? Com execution caching do Vertex AI Pipelines, o passo de pré-processamento (entradas inalteradas) é reaproveitado e só o treino roda de novo, sem mudar a estrutura do pipeline. Parâmetros e passos extras (A) ou um novo pipeline com caminho fixo (B) aumentam as mudanças e a manutenção. pipeline caching, Vertex AI Pipelines, cost

You have been tasked with deploying prototype code to production. The feature engineering code is in PySpark and runs on Dataproc Serverless. The model training is executed by using a Vertex AI custom training job. The two steps are not connected, and the model training must currently be run manually after the feature engineering step finishes. You need to create a scalable and maintainable production process that runs end-to-end and tracks the connections between steps. What should you do? Um Vertex AI Pipeline com o componente Dataproc Serverless (Google Cloud Pipeline Components) e um componente de custom training conecta os passos, escala e registra a lineage. Notebooks (A, B) não são processo de produção, e rodar Spark dentro de um componente (D) perde o serverless e a escalabilidade. Vertex AI Pipelines, Dataproc Serverless, Google Cloud Pipeline Components

You developed a Vertex AI pipeline that trains a classification model on data stored in a large BigQuery table. The pipeline has four steps, where each step is created by a Python function that uses the KubeFlow v2 API. The components have the following names: You launch your Vertex AI pipeline as the following: You perform many model iterations by adjusting the code and parameters of the training step. You observe high costs associated with the development, particularly the data export and preprocessing steps. You need to reduce model development costs. What should you do? O enunciado original omite o código, mas as opções indicam que os nomes dos arquivos YAML dos componentes incluem o timestamp {dt}, o que muda a definição dos componentes a cada execução e impede o execution caching do Vertex AI Pipelines. Fixar os nomes de export e preprocess permite reaproveitar do cache esses passos caros, mantendo train/calibrate variáveis. O parâmetro kubeflow.v1.caching (B) não existe, e separar manualmente o primeiro passo (C) é mais trabalhoso do que usar o caching nativo. execution caching, Vertex AI Pipelines, KFP v2, custo

You recently developed a wide and deep model in TensorFlow. You generated training datasets using a SQL script that preprocessed raw data in BigQuery by performing instance-level transformations of the data. You need to create a training pipeline to retrain the model on a weekly basis. The trained model will be used to generate daily recommendations. You want to minimize model development and training time. How should you develop the training pipeline? Como o pré-processamento já existe em SQL no BigQuery, usar BigQueryJobOp para rodá-lo e CustomTrainingJobOp para treinar no Vertex AI reaproveita o que existe com mínimo de desenvolvimento. Reescrever o pré-processamento em Dataflow (B) ou em TFX Transform/input fn (C, D) aumenta o tempo de desenvolvimento sem necessidade, já que as transformações são instance-level. Vertex AI Pipelines, BigQueryJobOp, CustomTrainingJobOp, Google Cloud Pipeline Components

You have trained a model by using data that was preprocessed in a batch Dataflow pipeline. Your use case requires real-time inference. You want to ensure that the data preprocessing logic is applied consistently between training and serving. What should you do? Refatorar a lógica de transformação para um módulo reutilizável e usar o mesmo código no endpoint (por exemplo, em uma custom prediction routine) garante a mesma transformação em treino e serving, evitando training-serving skew. Compartilhar o código com os usuários finais (C) transfere a responsabilidade e gera inconsistência, e agrupar requisições em janelas no Dataflow (D) quebra a exigência de inferência em tempo real. training-serving skew, pré-processamento, custom prediction routine

You need to develop a custom TensorFlow model that will be used for online predictions. The training data is stored in BigQuery You need to apply instance-level data transformations to the data for model training and serving. You want to use the same preprocessing routine during model training and serving. How should you configure the preprocessing routine? TensorFlow Transform executado com Apache Beam no Dataflow gera um transform graph que é exportado junto com o SavedModel, aplicando exatamente o mesmo pré-processamento no treino e no serving online. Um script no BigQuery (A) ou componente de pipeline (B) só cobre o treino, e uma custom prediction routine (C) duplica a lógica no serving com risco de skew. TensorFlow Transform, Dataflow, training-serving skew, Apache Beam

You are building a TensorFlow text-to-image generative model by using a dataset that contains billions of images with their respective captions. You want to create a low maintenance, automated workflow that reads the data from a Cloud Storage bucket collects statistics, splits the dataset into training/validation/test datasets performs data transformations trains the model using the training/validation datasets, and validates the model by using the test dataset. What should you do? O fluxo pedido (ler dados, coletar estatísticas, dividir em train/val/test, transformar, treinar e validar) corresponde exatamente aos componentes padrão do TFX (ExampleGen, StatisticsGen, Transform, Trainer, Evaluator), e o Google recomenda TFX para modelos TensorFlow com grandes volumes de dados, executando no Vertex AI Pipelines com Dataflow. KFP (C, o gabarito) também funcionaria, mas exigiria implementar manualmente esses componentes, aumentando a manutenção; Composer e MLflow (A, B) não são a opção gerenciada recomendada. TFX, Vertex AI Pipelines, Dataflow, TensorFlow

You are developing an ML pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines. You want your pipeline to upload a new version of the XGBoost model to Vertex AI Model Registry and deploy it to Vertex AI Endpoints for online inference. You want to use the simplest approach. What should you do? Os Google Cloud Pipeline Components ModelUploadOp e ModelDeployOp encadeados fazem upload da nova versão ao Model Registry e o deploy no endpoint sem código customizado. Escrever um componente próprio com REST API ou SDK (A, C) funciona, mas é mais trabalhoso, e ModelEvaluationOp (B) só avalia o modelo. ModelUploadOp, ModelDeployOp, Model Registry, Vertex AI Pipelines

You are creating a model training pipeline to predict sentiment scores from text-based product reviews. You want to have control over how the model parameters are tuned, and you will deploy the model to an endpoint after it has been trained. You will use Vertex AI Pipelines to run the pipeline. You need to decide which Google Cloud pipeline components to use. What components should you choose? Dados de reviews são texto (TextDatasetCreateOp), o controle sobre o tuning dos parâmetros exige treino customizado (CustomTrainingJobOp), e ModelDeployOp implanta o modelo no endpoint. AutoML (B, C) não dá controle sobre os hiperparâmetros, e EndpointCreateOp (A, B) apenas cria o endpoint sem implantar o modelo. Google Cloud Pipeline Components, CustomTrainingJobOp, ModelDeployOp

You are building a custom image classification model and plan to use Vertex AI Pipelines to implement the end-to-end training. Your dataset consists of images that need to be preprocessed before they can be used to train the model. The preprocessing steps include resizing the images, converting them to grayscale, and extracting features. You have already implemented some Python functions for the preprocessing tasks. Which components should you use in your pipeline? DataflowPythonJobOp executa as funções Python de pré-processamento como um job Apache Beam escalável no Dataflow, WaitGcpResourcesOp aguarda o término do job, e CustomTrainingJobOp treina o modelo customizado. Usar componentes leves com dsl.ParallelFor (C) não escala bem para grandes volumes de imagens, Spark no Dataproc (A) exigiria reescrever o código e AutoML (D) contradiz o modelo customizado. DataflowPythonJobOp, WaitGcpResourcesOp, CustomTrainingJobOp, Vertex AI Pipelines

You are developing a training pipeline for a new XGBoost classification model based on tabular data. The data is stored in a BigQuery table. You need to complete the following steps: 1. Randomly split the data into training and evaluation datasets in a 65/35 ratio 2. Conduct feature engineering 3. Obtain metrics for the evaluation dataset 4. Compare models trained in different pipeline executions How should you execute these steps? Vertex AI Pipelines com componentes de split e feature engineering, autologging de métricas e comparação de runs no Vertex AI Experiments cobre todos os passos, incluindo comparar execuções diferentes do pipeline. As opções em BigQuery ML usam ML.TRAINING INFO, que retorna informações de iterações de treino, não métricas de avaliação para comparar modelos; B usa lineage, que não é feito para comparar métricas. Vertex AI Pipelines, Vertex AI Experiments, autologging, XGBoost

You have recently used TensorFlow to train a classification model on tabular data. You have created a Dataflow pipeline that can transform several terabytes of data into training or prediction datasets consisting of TFRecords. You now need to productionize the model, and you want the predictions to be automatically uploaded to a BigQuery table on a weekly schedule. What should you do? Para previsões semanais em lote basta importar o modelo e criar um pipeline com DataflowPythonJobOp (reaproveitando o pré-processamento) e ModelBatchPredictOp, que grava direto no BigQuery e pode ser agendado. Implantar em endpoint (A/B) mantém nós online ligados sem necessidade e B ainda exige código para enviar requisições; D reescreveria a lógica em SQL. Vertex AI Pipelines, batch prediction, Dataflow, BigQuery

You recently created a new Google Cloud project. After testing that you can submit a Vertex AI Pipeline job from the Cloud Shell, you want to use a Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebook instance to run your code from that instance. You created the instance and ran the code but this time the job fails with an insufficient permissions error. What should you do? O notebook roda com a service account da instância, que precisa do papel Vertex AI User para submeter jobs de pipeline; no Cloud Shell eram usadas as credenciais do usuário, por isso funcionou. Região ou sub-rede (A/B) gerariam outros erros, não de permissão, e Notebooks Runner não concede acesso ao Vertex AI Pipelines. IAM, service account, Vertex AI Pipelines, Workbench

You are creating an ML pipeline for data processing, model training, and model deployment that uses different Google Cloud services. You have developed code for each individual task, and you expect a high frequency of new files. You now need to create an orchestration layer on top of these tasks. You only want this orchestration pipeline to run if new files are present in your dataset in a Cloud Storage bucket. You also want to minimize the compute node costs. What should you do? Um Cloud Function acionado por evento do Cloud Storage dispara o Vertex AI pipeline só quando chega arquivo novo, e o Vertex AI Pipelines é serverless, sem nós ociosos. Cloud Composer (B/D) mantém um ambiente sempre ligado, gerando custo de compute; agendamento periódico (A) roda mesmo sem arquivos novos. Vertex AI Pipelines, Cloud Functions, event-driven, Cloud Storage trigger

You are using Kubeflow Pipelines to develop an end-to-end PyTorch-based MLOps pipeline. The pipeline reads data from BigQuery, processes the data, conducts feature engineering, model training, model evaluation, and deploys the model as a binary file to Cloud Storage. You are writing code for several different versions of the feature engineering and model training steps, and running each new version in Vertex AI Pipelines. Each pipeline run is taking over an hour to complete. You want to speed up the pipeline execution to reduce your development time, and you want to avoid additional costs. What should you do? Com caching habilitado, os passos cujas entradas e código não mudaram reutilizam saídas de execuções anteriores, acelerando o desenvolvimento sem custo extra. Comentar partes do pipeline (A) é frágil e quebra dependências; GPU (D) adiciona custo. Kubeflow Pipelines, caching, Vertex AI Pipelines

You work for a public transportation company and need to build a model to estimate delay times for multiple transportation routes. Predictions are served directly to users in an app in real time. Because different seasons and population increases impact the data relevance, you will retrain the model every month. You want to follow Google-recommended best practices. How should you configure the end-to-end architecture of the predictive model? Kubeflow Pipelines (hoje Vertex AI Pipelines) orquestra o fluxo de várias etapas do treino ao deploy com agendamento, a prática recomendada para retreino periódico. Cloud Functions com Scheduler (C) funciona mas é uma solução ad hoc sem rastreabilidade, e Dataflow (D) não é ferramenta de orquestração de treino. Kubeflow Pipelines, retraining, orquestração

You are developing ML models with AI Platform for image segmentation on CT scans. You frequently update your model architectures based on the newest available research papers, and have to rerun training on the same dataset to benchmark their performance. You want to minimize computation costs and manual intervention while having version control for your code. What should you do? Cloud Build com gatilho no repositório dá versionamento e dispara o retreino automaticamente só quando há push, minimizando custo e intervenção manual. Composer rodando diariamente (D) gasta recursos sem necessidade, e gcloud manual (B) não automatiza. Cloud Build, CI/CD, retraining

You have written unit tests for a Kubeflow Pipeline that require custom libraries. You want to automate the execution of unit tests with each new push to your development branch in Cloud Source Repositories. What should you do? Um gatilho do Cloud Build no push ao branch de desenvolvimento executa os testes automaticamente, solução gerenciada e com menos esforço. Sinks de Logging com Pub/Sub e Cloud Run/Functions (C, D) funcionam, mas são complexos e desnecessários. Cloud Build, unit tests, CI/CD

You work with a data engineering team that has developed a pipeline to clean your dataset and save it in a Cloud Storage bucket. You have created an ML model and want to use the data to refresh your model as soon as new data is available. As part of your CI/CD workflow, you want to automatically run a Kubeflow Pipelines training job on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). How should you architect this workflow? Notificação do Cloud Storage via Pub/Sub acionando uma Cloud Function para iniciar o pipeline é event-driven e dispara assim que chegam dados novos. Polling (B) ou agendamento (D) desperdiçam recursos e atrasam o retreino. event-driven, Pub/Sub, Cloud Functions, retraining

Your data science team has requested a system that supports scheduled model retraining, Docker containers, and a service that supports autoscaling and monitoring for online prediction requests. Which platform components should you choose for this system? Vertex AI Pipelines cobre o retreino agendado com containers, Vertex AI Prediction dá autoscaling no online serving e Model Monitoring cobre o monitoramento. App Engine e BigQuery ML (A, C, D) não atendem bem a todos os requisitos juntos. Vertex AI Pipelines, Vertex AI Prediction, Model Monitoring

You developed a Vertex AI ML pipeline that consists of preprocessing and training steps and each set of steps runs on a separate custom Docker image. Your organization uses GitHub and GitHub Actions as CI/CD to run unit and integration tests. You need to automate the model retraining workflow so that it can be initiated both manually and when a new version of the code is merged in the main branch. You want to minimize the steps required to build the workflow while also allowing for maximum flexibility. How should you configure the CI/CD workflow? Manter os testes no GitHub Actions, que a organização já usa (e que suporta workflow dispatch manual e gatilho de merge), e delegar o build das imagens ao Cloud Build, que é gerenciado e integrado ao Artifact Registry, dá flexibilidade com poucos passos. C é tentadora, mas fazer o build no runner do GitHub tira a integração nativa com o Google Cloud, e Cloud Run (B) não é ferramenta de build. CI/CD, GitHub Actions, Cloud Build, Artifact Registry

You recently deployed a pipeline in Vertex AI Pipelines that trains and pushes a model to a Vertex AI endpoint to serve real-time traffic. You need to continue experimenting and iterating on your pipeline to improve model performance. You plan to use Cloud Build for CI/CD You want to quickly and easily deploy new pipelines into production, and you want to minimize the chance that the new pipeline implementations will break in production. What should you do? O CI/CD deve buildar e testar, implantar em pré-produção e promover os mesmos artefatos para produção após uma execução bem-sucedida do pipeline. Rebuildar para produção (D) pode gerar artefatos diferentes dos testados, e o upload manual pelo console (A) não é automação. CI/CD, Cloud Build, pre-production

You have developed a BigQuery ML model that predicts customer chum, and deployed the model to Vertex AI Endpoints. You want to automate the retraining of your model by using minimal additional code when model feature values change. You also want to minimize the number of times that your model is retrained to reduce training costs. What should you do? Como o modelo do BigQuery ML tem os dados de treino acessíveis, o Model Monitoring de training-serving skew compara direto com esse baseline e dispara retreino via Pub/Sub e Cloud Function só quando há desvio significativo, com código mínimo. Jobs de TFDV agendados (A, B) exigem código custom, e drift (C) compara janelas de serving entre si, o que pode disparar mais retreinos. Model Monitoring, training-serving skew, Pub/Sub, Cloud Functions

Your team has a model deployed to a Vertex AI endpoint. You have created a Vertex AI pipeline that automates the model training process and is triggered by a Cloud Function. You need to prioritize keeping the model up-to-date, but also minimize retraining costs. How should you configure retraining? Disparar o retreino só quando o Model Monitoring detecta feature drift mantém o modelo atualizado e evita retreinos desnecessários. Agendamento fixo (B) pode retreinar sem necessidade ou tarde demais, e apenas ter dados novos (A) não indica que o modelo degradou. Model Monitoring, feature drift, retraining, Pub/Sub

Your team frequently creates new ML models and runs experiments. Your team pushes code to a single repository hosted on Cloud Source Repositories. You want to create a continuous integration pipeline that automatically retrains the models whenever there is any modification of the code. What should be your first step to set up the CI pipeline? Um Cloud Build trigger com evento 'Push to a branch' dispara a cada modificação de código enviada ao repositório, base de um pipeline de CI que retreina os modelos. O trigger de Pull Request (A) não cobre todos os pushes (e não é suportado no Cloud Source Repositories), e Cloud Functions (C, D) seriam uma solução improvisada em vez do serviço de CI gerenciado. Cloud Build, CI/CD, trigger, retreino

You work for a pharmaceutical company based in Canada. Your team developed a BigQuery ML model to predict the number of flu infections for the next month in Canada. Weather data is published weekly, and flu infection statistics are published monthly. You need to configure a model retraining policy that minimizes cost. What should you do? Retreinar apenas quando o monitoramento de feature drift indicar mudança evita retreinos desnecessários, e baixar cada fonte na cadência em que é publicada (clima semanal, gripe mensal) evita downloads inúteis, minimizando custo. Retreinar em agenda fixa (A, B, C) gasta recursos mesmo sem mudança nos dados, e baixar dados de gripe semanalmente (A, C) não traz dados novos. retreino, feature drift, Model Monitoring, custo

ou are developing an ML model that predicts the cost of used automobiles based on data such as location, condition, model type, color, and engine/battery efficiency. The data is updated every night. Car dealerships will use the model to determine appropriate car prices. You created a Vertex AI pipeline that reads the data splits the data into training/evaluation/test sets performs feature engineering trains the model by using the training dataset and validates the model by using the evaluation dataset. You need to configure a retraining workflow that minimizes cost. What should you do? Comparar com a avaliação do run anterior garante que só um modelo melhor seja implantado, e disparar o retreino apenas quando o monitoramento de skew ultrapassa o limite evita custo de rodar o pipeline toda noite. Comparar losses de treino/avaliação do mesmo run só detecta overfitting, e o cron noturno gera custo desnecessário. retreino, Model Monitoring, training-serving skew, custo

You created a model that uses BigQuery ML to perform linear regression. You need to retrain the model on the cumulative data collected every week. You want to minimize the development effort and the scheduling cost. What should you do? Scheduled queries do BigQuery executam o CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL periodicamente sem código adicional e sem custo extra de agendamento. Pipelines, Cloud Functions ou Workflows com Cloud Scheduler adicionam componentes e esforço desnecessários. BigQuery ML, scheduled queries, retreino

You work on a growing team of more than 50 data scientists who all use AI Platform. You are designing a strategy to organize your jobs, models, and versions in a clean and scalable way. Which strategy should you choose? Labels são a forma recomendada e escalável de organizar jobs, models e versions, permitindo filtrar recursos por equipe, projeto ou dono. Separar cada cientista em um projeto (B) fragmenta a colaboração e não escala; IAM restritivo (A) trata de acesso, não de organização. labels, organização de recursos, Vertex AI

You are a lead ML engineer at a retail company. You want to track and manage ML metadata in a centralized way so that your team can have reproducible experiments by generating artifacts. Which management solution should you recommend to your team? Vertex ML Metadata é o serviço gerenciado para rastrear artefatos, execuções e linhagem, garantindo reprodutibilidade. O gabarito B (Hive Metastore) está errado: ele guarda metadados de tabelas Hive, não metadados de ML; operations suite e BigQuery (A, C) também não são feitos para isso. Vertex ML Metadata, linhagem, reprodutibilidade

You are an ML engineer at a travel company. You have been researching customers’ travel behavior for many years, and you have deployed models that predict customers’ vacation patterns. You have observed that customers’ vacation destinations vary based on seasonality and holidays; however, these seasonal variations are similar across years. You want to quickly and easily store and compare the model versions and performance statistics across years. What should you do? Vertex ML Metadata permite registrar estatísticas de desempenho de cada versão com atributos (temporada, ano) e compará-las de forma estruturada, preservando linhagem. A opção B (versões no Vertex AI e aba Evaluate) é tentadora, mas criar uma versão por temporada/ano e comparar manualmente na UI é menos flexível para comparações entre anos; a comunidade fica dividida entre as duas. Vertex ML Metadata, versionamento, comparação de modelos

You are developing a process for training and running your custom model in production. You need to be able to show lineage for your model and predictions. What should you do? Executar o treino e a batch prediction como componentes do Vertex AI Pipelines registra automaticamente artefatos e execuções no Vertex ML Metadata, gerando linhagem de dataset, modelo e predições. A opção A (managed dataset + training pipeline) é tentadora, mas fora de um pipeline a linhagem das predições não fica conectada de ponta a ponta; Experiments (D) rastreia métricas, não a linhagem completa. lineage, Vertex AI Pipelines, Vertex ML Metadata, batch prediction

You are building a MLOps platform to automate your company’s ML experiments and model retraining. You need to organize the artifacts for dozens of pipelines. How should you store the pipelines’ artifacts? Parâmetros e metadados das execuções vão para o Vertex ML Metadata (com linhagem), código-fonte fica no controle de versão (GitHub) e binários dos modelos no Cloud Storage, que é o armazenamento adequado a artefatos grandes. Guardar binários no GitHub (A, D) é inadequado, e Cloud SQL (A, B) exige construir e manter um esquema próprio de metadados. Vertex ML Metadata, artefatos, Cloud Storage, MLOps

You are investigating the root cause of a misclassification error made by one of your models. You used Vertex AI Pipelines to train and deploy the model. The pipeline reads data from BigQuery. creates a copy of the data in Cloud Storage in TFRecord format, trains the model in Vertex AI Training on that copy, and deploys the model to a Vertex AI endpoint. You have identified the specific version of that model that misclassified, and you need to recover the data this model was trained on. How should you find that copy of the data? O Vertex ML Metadata registra a linhagem dos artefatos de cada execução do Vertex AI Pipelines, permitindo partir da versão do modelo e chegar ao artefato de dados TFRecord gerado pelo passo de cópia e à sua localização no Cloud Storage. Procurar em logs por timestamps (C, D) é frágil e manual, e Feature Store (A) exigiria mudar o pipeline e não recupera a cópia histórica. lineage, Vertex ML Metadata, Vertex AI Pipelines, artefatos

You have a custom job that runs on Vertex AI on a weekly basis. The job is implemented using a proprietary ML workflow that produces the datasets, models, and custom artifacts, and sends them to a Cloud Storage bucket. Many different versions of the datasets and models were created. Due to compliance requirements, your company needs to track which model was used for making a particular prediction, and needs access to the artifacts for each model. How should you configure your workflows to meet these requirements? Usar a Vertex ML Metadata API dentro do custom job para criar contexts, executions e artifacts ligados por events registra a linhagem completa de dataset, modelo e artefatos customizados, permitindo saber qual modelo gerou cada previsão. Labels no Model Registry (D) não rastreiam linhagem, e um ML Metadata TFX próprio (C) exige gerenciar infraestrutura. Vertex ML Metadata, lineage, compliance

You are an ML engineer at a regulated insurance company. You are asked to develop an insurance approval model that accepts or rejects insurance applications from potential customers. What factors should you consider before building the model? Em setor regulado, decisões de aprovação precisam ser rastreáveis, reproduzíveis e explicáveis para auditoria. Federated learning e differential privacy (C, D) são técnicas de privacidade e não requisitos centrais aqui; redaction (A) não é o foco. explainability, traceability, reproducibility, regulated industry

You work at a subscription-based company. You have trained an ensemble of trees and neural networks to predict customer churn, which is the likelihood that customers will not renew their yearly subscription. The average prediction is a 15% churn rate, but for a particular customer the model predicts that they are 70% likely to churn. The customer has a product usage history of 30%, is located in New York City, and became a customer in 1997. You need to explain the difference between the actual prediction, a 70% churn rate, and the average prediction. You want to use Vertex Explainable AI. What should you do? Sampled Shapley atribui a diferença entre a predição e o baseline às features e funciona com modelos não diferenciáveis, como ensemble com árvores. Integrated gradients (C) é tentador, mas exige modelo diferenciável. Vertex Explainable AI, sampled Shapley, feature attribution

You are an ML engineer at a bank. You have developed a binary classification model using AutoML Tables to predict whether a customer will make loan payments on time. The output is used to approve or reject loan requests. One customer’s loan request has been rejected by your model, and the bank’s risks department is asking you to provide the reasons that contributed to the model’s decision. What should you do? Explicar uma decisão individual pede local feature importance (feature attributions da própria predição). A importância global da página de avaliação (C) é tentadora, mas descreve o modelo como um todo, não esse cliente. local feature importance, explicabilidade, AutoML

You work for a magazine distributor and need to build a model that predicts which customers will renew their subscriptions for the upcoming year. Using your company’s historical data as your training set, you created a TensorFlow model and deployed it to AI Platform. You need to determine which customer attribute has the most predictive power for each prediction served by the model. What should you do? AI Explanations com sampled Shapley devolve atribuições por feature para cada predição servida, exatamente o que foi pedido. O What-If Tool e a correlação (B, D) dão visão global ou exploratória, não a atribuição de cada request. AI Explanations, sampled Shapley, feature attribution

You work for a gaming company that has millions of customers around the world. All games offer a chat feature that allows players to communicate with each other in real time. Messages can be typed in more than 20 languages and are translated in real time using the Cloud Translation API. You have been asked to build an ML system to moderate the chat in real time while assuring that the performance is uniform across the various languages and without changing the serving infrastructure. You trained your first model using an in-house word2vec model for embedding the chat messages translated by the Cloud Translation API. However, the model has significant differences in performance across the different languages. How should you improve it? A diferença de desempenho entre idiomas vem do ruído introduzido pela tradução automática antes do embedding; treinar o classificador nos textos no idioma original remove essa fonte de viés. Min-Diff (A) é tentador por ser técnica de fairness, mas não ataca a causa raiz, e trocar por GPT-3/T5 (C) mudaria a infraestrutura de serving. fairness, Cloud Translation API, viés entre idiomas

You are an ML engineer at a bank that has a mobile application. Management has asked you to build an ML-based biometric authentication for the app that verifies a customer’s identity based on their fingerprint. Fingerprints are considered highly sensitive personal information and cannot be downloaded and stored into the bank databases. Which learning strategy should you recommend to train and deploy this ML mode? Federated learning treina o modelo nos dispositivos dos usuários e envia apenas atualizações de pesos, então as impressões digitais nunca saem do celular. Differential privacy (D) é tentadora, mas pressupõe que os dados sejam coletados centralmente, o que é proibido aqui; DLP e MD5 não são estratégias de aprendizado. federated learning, privacidade, dados biométricos

You are an ML engineer in the contact center of a large enterprise. You need to build a sentiment analysis tool that predicts customer sentiment from recorded phone conversations. You need to identify the best approach to building a model while ensuring that the gender, age, and cultural differences of the customers who called the contact center do not impact any stage of the model development pipeline and results. What should you do? Converter a fala em texto remove características de voz (tom, sotaque) ligadas a gênero, idade e cultura, e analisar sentimento por sentença captura o contexto melhor do que palavras isoladas. A opção B é tentadora, mas modelos baseados em palavras isoladas perdem contexto e podem carregar vieses de vocabulário; extrair direto do áudio (C) introduz viés de voz. fairness, Speech-to-Text, sentiment analysis

You work for a retailer that sells clothes to customers around the world. You have been tasked with ensuring that ML models are built in a secure manner. Specifically, you need to protect sensitive customer data that might be used in the models. You have identified four fields containing sensitive data that are being used by your data science team: AGE, IS EXISTING CUSTOMER, LATITUDE LONGITUDE, and SHIRT SIZE. What should you do with the data before it is made available to the data science team for training purposes? Tokenizar os campos com valores substitutos (hashing) remove os valores sensíveis reais e mantém a utilidade dos campos como features categóricas para o modelo. Coarsening (C) é tentador por ser técnica válida de desidentificação, mas não protege todos os campos e a granularidade proposta ainda pode reidentificar; remover tudo (D) perde sinal preditivo. desidentificação, tokenização, Cloud DLP

You recently deployed an ML model. Three months after deployment, you notice that your model is underperforming on certain subgroups, thus potentially leading to biased results. You suspect that the inequitable performance is due to class imbalances in the training data, but you cannot collect more data. What should you do? (Choose two.) Sem coletar mais dados, as saídas clássicas para desbalanceamento são reponderar a loss para punir mais erros na classe minoritária (B) e fazer upsampling/reweighting dos exemplos existentes (D). Remover exemplos de bom desempenho (A) joga fora informação, e remover features correlacionadas (C) não corrige o desbalanceamento. fairness, class imbalance, reweighting, upsampling

Your organization manages an online message board. A few months ago, you discovered an increase in toxic language and bullying on the message board. You deployed an automated text classifier that flags certain comments as toxic or harmful. Now some users are reporting that benign comments referencing their religion are being misclassified as abusive. Upon further inspection, you find that your classifier's false positive rate is higher for comments that reference certain underrepresented religious groups. Your team has a limited budget and is already overextended. What should you do? Com orçamento limitado e equipe sobrecarregada, ajustar o threshold é a ação mais barata e imediata para reduzir os falsos positivos. Dados sintéticos (A) atacam melhor a causa do viés e são a alternativa mais tentadora, mas exigem geração de dados e retreino, que a equipe não tem como bancar agora. Moderação humana ou trocar de modelo (B, C) são caros. fairness, false positive rate, threshold

You work for a magazine distributor and need to build a model that predicts which customers will renew their subscriptions for the upcoming year. Using your company’s historical data as your training set, you created a TensorFlow model and deployed it to Vertex AI. You need to determine which customer attribute has the most predictive power for each prediction served by the model. What should you do? Vertex Explainable AI devolve feature attributions por predição (sampled Shapley) com o método explain, exatamente o que se pede: importância por predição. Correlação de Pearson (A) e Lasso (C) são globais, e o What-If Tool (D) não gera atribuições por requisição em produção. Vertex Explainable AI, sampled Shapley, feature attributions

You work for a bank. You have created a custom model to predict whether a loan application should be flagged for human review. The input features are stored in a BigQuery table. The model is performing well, and you plan to deploy it to production. Due to compliance requirements the model must provide explanations for each prediction. You want to add this functionality to your model code with minimal effort and provide explanations that are as accurate as possible. What should you do? Subir o modelo custom no Model Registry com explanation config (sampled Shapley e input baselines) ativa o Vertex Explainable AI sem alterar o código do modelo. Trocar por AutoML ou BigQuery ML (A, B) descarta o modelo validado, e implementar Shapley no container (D) dá muito trabalho. Vertex Explainable AI, sampled Shapley, Model Registry

You work for a retail company. You have created a Vertex AI forecast model that produces monthly item sales predictions. You want to quickly create a report that will help to explain how the model calculates the predictions. You have one month of recent actual sales data that was not included in the training dataset. How should you generate data for your report? Uma batch prediction com feature attributions mostra quanto cada feature contribuiu para cada previsão, o que explica como o modelo calcula as previsões. Comparar só previsões com valores reais (A) mede acurácia, não explicação. Counterfactuals ou treinar um modelo ablado (C, D) dão mais trabalho. Vertex Explainable AI, batch prediction, feature attributions, forecasting

You are building a predictive maintenance model to preemptively detect part defects in bridges. You plan to use high definition images of the bridges as model inputs. You need to explain the output of the model to the relevant stakeholders so they can take appropriate action. How should you build the model? Para imagens de alta resolução, um modelo de deep learning em TensorFlow é o adequado, e Integrated Gradients é o método de feature attribution diferenciável recomendado pelo Vertex Explainable AI para imagens, gerando mapas de saliência por pixel. Sampled Shapley (D) é indicado para modelos não diferenciáveis e é muito caro com milhões de pixels; modelos de árvore no scikit-learn (A, B) não são adequados para imagens brutas. Integrated Gradients, Explainable AI, imagens, deep learning

You work for a telecommunications company. You’re building a model to predict which customers may fail to pay their next phone bill. The purpose of this model is to proactively offer at-risk customers assistance such as service discounts and bill deadline extensions. The data is stored in BigQuery and the predictive features that are available for model training include: - Customer id - Age - Salary (measured in local currency) - Sex - Average bill value (measured in local currency) - Number of phone calls in the last month (integer) - Average duration of phone calls (measured in minutes) You need to investigate and mitigate potential bias against disadvantaged groups, while preserving model accuracy. What should you do? Definir uma métrica de fairness (por exemplo, acurácia por grupo sensível), avaliar o modelo no test set e juntar os resultados com os atributos sensíveis permite investigar o viés de forma direta, sem sacrificar acurácia de antemão. Remover features sensíveis e correlacionadas (A) é tentador, mas reduz acurácia e não garante fairness (proxies permanecem); usar attributions (B, C) mede importância, não viés contra grupos. fairness, viés, métricas por grupo, BigQuer

You work for a manufacturing company. You need to train a custom image classification model to detect product defects at the end of an assembly line. Although your model is performing well, some images in your holdout set are consistently mislabeled with high confidence. You want to use Vertex AI to understand your model’s results. What should you do? Imagens classificadas erradas com alta confiança sugerem problemas nos dados de treino (rótulos errados ou exemplos semelhantes mal rotulados), e example-based explanations do Vertex AI recuperam os exemplos de treino mais próximos no espaço latente, que é exatamente o caso de uso documentado pelo Google para encontrar dados mal rotulados. O gabarito A (Integrated Gradients com PIXELS) mostra quais pixels influenciaram a predição, mas não explica por que o modelo está confiante no rótulo errado; o Matching Engine (B) é só um índice de vetores, sem a integração de explicação. example-based explanations, Explainable AI, dados mal rotulados, espaço latente

You are using Vertex AI and TensorFlow to develop a custom image classification model. You need the model’s decisions and the rationale to be understandable to your company’s stakeholders. You also want to explore the results to identify any issues or potential biases. What should you do? Gerar feature attributions com o Vertex Explainable AI e agregá-las em todo o dataset mostra em que o modelo se baseia de forma global, permitindo comunicar a lógica aos stakeholders e identificar vieses, junto com as métricas de avaliação. Example-based explanations (C) mostram exemplos semelhantes, mas não explicam o raciocínio do modelo; o TensorFlow Profiler (B) trata de performance, não de interpretabilidade. feature attributions, Explainable AI, viés, stakeholders

You work for a retail company. You have been tasked with building a model to determine the probability of churn for each customer. You need the predictions to be interpretable so the results can be used to develop marketing campaigns that target at-risk customers. What should you do? AutoML tabular com explanations por previsão dá atribuições locais para cada cliente, permitindo entender por que cada um está em risco e montar campanhas direcionadas, com pouco esforço. Random forest com feature importance (D) é tentador por ser classificação, mas só oferece importância global, não explicação individual. Explainable AI, AutoML, feature attribution, churn

You are developing a model to help your company create more targeted online advertising campaigns. You need to create a dataset that you will use to train the model. You want to avoid creating or reinforcing unfair bias in the model. What should you do? (Choose two.) A questão pede duas respostas e o gabarito traz só D: amostragem estratificada garante representação dos grupos no dataset, e testes de fairness por categorias sensíveis (E) verificam se o modelo treinado não reforça viés. Amostra aleatória (C) pode sub-representar grupos minoritários, e restringir aos grupos que mais interagem (B) reforça o viés. fairness, stratified sampling, bias, Responsible AI

You work for an online retail company that is creating a visual search engine. You have set up an end-to-end ML pipeline on Google Cloud to classify whether an image contains your company's product. Expecting the release of new products in the near future, you configured a retraining functionality in the pipeline so that new data can be fed into your ML models. You also want to use AI Platform's continuous evaluation service to ensure that the models have high accuracy on your test dataset. What should you do? O conjunto de teste deve ser estendido com imagens dos novos produtos para que a avaliação represente a distribuição atual, sem perder a cobertura dos produtos antigos. Substituir (C) perderia os produtos antigos, e manter inalterado (A) não mede o desempenho nos produtos novos. continuous evaluation, test set, retraining

You built and manage a production system that is responsible for predicting sales numbers. Model accuracy is crucial, because the production model is required to keep up with market changes. Since being deployed to production, the model hasn't changed; however the accuracy of the model has steadily deteriorated. What issue is most likely causing the steady decline in model accuracy? Um modelo que nunca é retreinado sofre com drift à medida que o mercado muda, o que explica a queda gradual. Má qualidade de dados (A) é tentadora, mas causaria problemas desde o início, não uma deterioração contínua. model drift, retraining, monitoring

You have deployed multiple versions of an image classification model on AI Platform. You want to monitor the performance of the model versions over time. How should you perform this comparison? O Continuous Evaluation compara versões ao longo do tempo com dados de produção rotulados, usando métricas como mean average precision. Comparar loss em held-out ou validação (A, B) é uma avaliação pontual, e o What-If Tool (C) não monitora ao longo do tempo. continuous evaluation, mAP, model versions

Your team trained and tested a DNN regression model with good results. Six months after deployment, the model is performing poorly due to a change in the distribution of the input data. How should you address the input differences in production? Mudança na distribuição de entrada deve ser detectada com alertas de skew/drift e tratada com retreino nos dados recentes. Seleção de features ou regularização (B, C, D) não resolvem a mudança de distribuição. data drift, skew monitoring, retraining

You recently joined a machine learning team that will soon release a new project. As a lead on the project, you are asked to determine the production readiness of the ML components. The team has already tested features and data, model development, and infrastructure. Which additional readiness check should you recommend to the team? O ML Test Score do Google tem quatro grupos: features e dados, desenvolvimento do modelo, infraestrutura e monitoramento; o que falta é monitorar o modelo em produção. Reprodutibilidade e schema (A, D) parecem boas checagens, mas pertencem às categorias já testadas. production readiness, ML Test Score, monitoring

You work for a large social network service provider whose users post articles and discuss news. Millions of comments are posted online each day, and more than 200 human moderators constantly review comments and flag those that are inappropriate. Your team is building an ML model to help human moderators check content on the platform. The model scores each comment and flags suspicious comments to be reviewed by a human. Which metric(s) should you use to monitor the model’s performance? Uma amostra aleatória de mensagens brutas revisada por humanos permite estimar precision e recall, porque inclui também o que o modelo deixou de sinalizar. A opção D, a mais votada, é tentadora pelo volume menor, mas só mede precision: sem ver os não sinalizados não há como estimar false negatives nem recall. precision, recall, monitoramento com humanos

You have successfully deployed to production a large and complex TensorFlow model trained on tabular data. You want to predict the lifetime value (LTV) field for each subscription stored in the BigQuery table named subscription. subscriptionPurchase in the project named my-fortune500-company-project. You have organized all your training code, from preprocessing data from the BigQuery table up to deploying the validated model to the Vertex AI endpoint, into a TensorFlow Extended (TFX) pipeline. You want to prevent prediction drift, i.e., a situation when a feature data distribution in production changes significantly over time. What should you do? Vertex AI Model Monitoring detecta drift das features comparando a distribuição em produção; amostrar 10% a cada 24 horas é suficiente para drift, que ocorre gradualmente, e mantém o custo baixo.
